Gentlemen :

This refers to your letter dated December 19, 2022, applying on behalf of THE ENGLISH CHERRIES, INC. for the issuance of a certificate of tax exemption enjoyed by a non-stock, non-profit corporation or association organized and operated exclusively for educational purposes under Section 30 (H) of the National Internal Revenue Code (Tax Code) of 1997, as amended. HTcADC

It is represented that THE ENGLISH CHERRIES, INC.,with Taxpayer Identification No. 000-000-000-000, is a non-stock, non-profit association duly organized and existing under the laws of the Republic of the Philippines and that it is registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission under Company Registration No. CN201822184.

In reply, please be informed that paragraph 3, Section 4, Article XIV of the 1987 Constitution states that:

"All revenues and assets of non-stock, non-profit educational institutions used actually, directly, and exclusively for educational purposes shall be exempt from taxes and duties."

Similarly, Section 30 (H) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended, provides, viz.:

"Sec. 30. Exemptions from Tax on Corporations. — The following organizations shall not be taxed under this Title in respect to income received by them as such:

xxx xxx xxx

(H) A non-stock and non-profit educational institution";

Moreover, there are two requisites in order for a non-stock, non-profit educational institution to be exempt from tax as provided under Revenue Memorandum Order No. 44-2016; to wit:

a) It is a non-stock, non-profit educational institution; and

b) Its revenues are actually, directly and exclusively used for educational purposes.

"Non-stock" means "no part of its income is distributable as dividends to its members, trustees, or officers" and that any profit "obtained as an incident to its operations shall, whenever necessary or proper, be used for the furtherance of the purpose or purposes for which the corporation was organized." [1] Meanwhile, "Non-profit" means that "no net income or asset accrues to or benefits any member or specific person, with all the net income or asset devoted to the institution's purposes and all its activities conducted not for profit." [2]

Based on the documents submitted by THE ENGLISH CHERRIES, INC.,the following was disclosed, to wit:

"The Trustees shall not receive any compensation, as such trustees, except for reasonable per diems. Any compensation may be granted to trustees by the vote of the members representing at least a majority of the membership at a regular or special members' meeting. In no case shall the total yearly compensation of trustees, as such trustees, exceed ten (10%) percent of the net income before income tax of the corporation during the preceding year."

The giving of per diems to the Officers is considered as distribution of equity (including the net income) of THE ENGLISH CHERRIES, INC. This is a form of private inurement which the law prohibits in the organization and operation of a non-stock, non-profit corporation. This act violates the requirement that no part of the net income or assets of the corporation shall inure to the benefit of any individual or specific person. Thus, THE ENGLISH CHERRIES, INC. cannot qualify as a non-stock, non-profit educational institution exempt from Income Tax under Section 30 (H) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended. CAIHTE

Please bear in mind that, "being a non-stock and/or non-profit corporation does not, by this reason alone, completely exempt an institution from tax." [3] Thus, "statutes granting tax exemptions are construed strictissimi juris against the taxpayer and liberally in favor of the taxing authority. A claim of tax exemption must be clearly shown and based on language in law too plain to be mistaken. Otherwise stated, taxation is the rule, exemption is the exception. The burden of proof rests upon the party claiming the exemption to prove that it is in fact covered by the exemption so claimed." [4] (BIR Ruling No. 466-2014 dated November 19, 2014)

In view of the foregoing, the request of THE ENGLISH CHERRIES, INC. to be exempted from income tax under Section 30 (H) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended is hereby denied as it failed to prove that it is a non-profit corporation. Therefore, THE ENGLISH CHERRIES, INC. shall be treated as an ordinary corporation subject to twenty-five percent (25%) or twenty percent (20%) income tax rate [5] pursuant to Section 27 (A) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended.

Please be guided accordingly.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request for confirmatory ruling on behalf of your client, PROCTER & GAMBLE PHILIPPINES, INC. (the "Company") that the transfer of club membership shares in the Manila Polo Club (MPC) is exempt from capital gains tax (CGT),donor's tax, and documentary stamp tax (DST).

Background

1. As represented, the Company is a stock corporation duly organized and existing under and by virtue of the laws of the Republic of the Philippines. CAacTH

2. The Company owns club membership shares in MPC. To avail of the privileges of the club, individual proprietary shares were issued to its employees (the "former nominees").These are evidenced by (a) the Deeds of Declaration of Trust executed by the employees, (b) Certificates of Lateral Transfer executed by the Company in favor of the employees, and (c) Proprietary Membership Certificates (PMC),as follows:

August 16, 2019

3. Once the employees end their employment in the Company, the abovementioned club shares will be transferred to a new set of employees as evidenced by the following:

Former Nominees

New Nominees

May 21, 2024

4. The registration of shares under the names of the Company's nominees is necessary as only natural persons are allowed to be admitted as a proprietary member of MPC.

5. The Company maintains that the above-described transfers are without consideration and are meant to implement the enjoyment of the benefits of the Company's employees, as a result of being members of MPC. cEaSHC

Discussion/Ruling

The transfer of MPC shares from the Transferors
to the Transferees is not subject to CGT.

A declaration of trust has been defined as an act by which a person acknowledges that the property, title to which he holds, is held by him for the use of another. [2]

In the Declaration of Trust, which the declarants/appointees executed, they acknowledged that the transfer did not give them any kind of right, claim, or interest whatsoever in the MPC shares and that they are holding only the legal ownership of the same with the beneficial ownership pertaining to the Company. Here, the Trustor is the Company while the Trustees are the declarants/appointees.

In the case of Sime Darby Pilipinas, Inc. v. Mendoza,[3] Sime Darby acquired a Class "A" club share in Alabang Country Club (ACC) in 1987, but being a corporation which was expressly disallowed by ACC's By-Laws to acquire and register the club share under its name, registered the share under the name of respondent Mendoza, Sime Darby's sales manager at the time. The Supreme Court held that a trust arrangement existed between Sime Darby and Mendoza and while the share was bought by Sime Darby and placed under the name of Mendoza, the latter's title was only limited to the use and enjoyment of the club's facilities and privileges while employed with the company.

In the instant case, the Company, the purchaser of the MPC shares, intends to give its legal title to its Trustee-appointees, which entitle the Trustee-appointees only to the use and enjoyment of the club's facilities since under the Articles of Incorporation and By-laws of MPC only natural persons may become registered members. Thus, the transfers of the legal title of the MPC shares from the former Trustee-appointees to the new Trustee-appointees are not subject to CGT under Section 24 (C) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997 (Tax Code),as amended, considering that the transfers involve neither monetary consideration nor change in beneficial ownership. IAETDc

The transfer is not subject to donor's tax.

Well-settled in our jurisprudence is the fact that the essential elements of a valid donation are: (1) the reduction of the patrimony of the donor; (2) the increase in the patrimony of the donee; and (3) the intent to do an act of liberality (animus donandi).[3]

Clearly, there is no intention on the part of the Company to donate to the new Trustee-appointees the MPC shares since the transactions are purely for a legitimate business purpose. Thus, the transfers will not be subject to donor's tax since there is no intention to donate, and the transactions are bona fide transactions effected solely for business reasons.

The transfer is not subject to DST.

The transfer is not subject to DST under Section 175 of the Tax Code, as amended. The rule in this jurisdiction is that the assignment of shares of stock of a domestic corporation is subject to DST upon execution of the deed transferring ownership or rights thereto, or upon delivery, assignment or indorsement of such shares in favor of another.

Revenue Regulations (RR) No. 13-2004, implementing the provisions of Republic Act (RA) No. 9243, otherwise known as "An Act Rationalizing the Provisions on the Documentary Stamp Tax of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, and for Other Purposes" qualified this rule by stating that for a sale or exchange to be taxable, there must be an actual or constructive transfer of beneficial ownership of the shares of stock from one person to another. Section 4 thereof provides:

"For a sale or exchange to be taxable, there must be an actual or constructive transfer of beneficial ownership of the shares of stock from one person to another. Such transfer may be manifested by the clear exercise of attributes of ownership over such stocks by the transferee, or by an actual entry of a change in the name appearing in the certificate of stock or in the Stock and Transfer Book of the issuing corporation or by any entry indicating transfer of beneficial ownership in any form of registry including those of a duly authorized scripless registry, such as those maintained for or by the Philippine Stock Exchange. However, if by the transfer of certificates of stock from a resigned trustee to a newly appointed trustee such certificate of stock remain in the name of the cestui que trust or the resigned trustee so that the new trustee is constituted as mere depository of the stock, such transfer is not taxable. Provided, however, that transfer of shares to 'nominees' to qualify them to sit in the board or to qualify them to perform any act in relation to the corporation shall not be subject to the DST provided herein only upon proof of a duly executed Nominee Agreement showing the purpose of the transfer; that the transfer is without consideration other than the undertaking of the nominee to only represent the beneficial owner of the stock; and the transfer is in trust." (Underscoring supplied.)

THEREFORE, the herein transfers cannot be subject to DST as there is no transfer or conveyance to the new trustees of the beneficial ownership of any right, claim or interest over the MPC shares or over the assets of MPC. There being no new conveyance to speak of in this case, there is no new exercise of a privilege upon which DST may be imposed. CTIEac

However, the notarial acknowledgment to the Deed of Declaration of Trust is subject to DST imposed under Section 188 of the Tax Code, as amended.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be ascertained that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Gentlemen :

This refers to your letter requesting for the renewal/revalidation of the ruling issued to Berthaphil, Inc. on July 26, 2001. HTcADC

It is represented that Berthaphil, Inc. (Berthaphil) is a domestic market enterprise duly registered with the Clark Freeport Zone (CFZ) engaged in industrial development within the CFZ. It constructs buildings and leases them out to locators engaged in manufacturing, warehousing, and Business Process Outsourcing activities. Berthaphil is enjoying a preferential tax rate of 5% in lieu of all national and local taxes under Republic Act (RA) No. 7227, as amended by RA No. 9400.

On July 26, 2001, the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) issued BIR Ruling DA-131-2001, wherein the BIR held that Berthaphil's lessees are not required to withhold 5% creditable withholding tax on rental payments for the lease of Berthaphil's property. At present, however, Berthaphil's lessees refuse to recognize the previous ruling and are requesting for an updated one. The said lessees are CFZ locators who are also enjoying a preferential tax rate of 5%.

In light of the foregoing, Berthaphil now requests for the renewal/revalidation of its exemption from the 5% creditable withholding tax on rental payments for the lease of its properties.

In reply, please be informed of Section 2.57.5 (B) (2) of Revenue Regulations No. 2-98, as amended, to wit:

"Sec. 2.57.5. Exemption from Withholding. — The withholding of creditable withholding tax prescribed in these Regulations shall not apply to income payments made to the following:

(A) x x x

(B) Persons enjoying exemption from payment of income taxes pursuant to the provisions of any law, general or special, such as but not limited to the following:

(1) x x x

(2) Corporations duly registered with the Board of Investments, Philippine Export Processing Zones and Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority enjoying exemption from the income tax pursuant to E.O. 226, as amended, RA 7916 and the Omnibus Investment Code of 1987 and R.A. 7227, as amended, respectively"; (Emphasis and underscoring supplied)

However, please note that under the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended by the CREATE Act, [1] the preferential tax rate of 5% on gross income earned extends only to registered export enterprises. [2] Nevertheless, domestic market enterprises availing of the 5% preferential tax rate prior to the effectivity of the CREATE Act are allowed to continue availing of such preferential tax rate for a period of ten (10) years.

Section 311 (C) of the Tax Code, as amended by the CREATE Act, provides:

"Sec. 311. Investments Prior to the Effectivity of this Act. — Registered business enterprises with incentives granted prior to the effectivity of this Act shall be subject to the following rules:

xxx xxx xxx

(C) Registered business enterprises currently availing of the five percent (5%) tax on gross income earned granted prior to the effectivity of this Act shall be allowed to continue availing the said tax incentive at the rate of five percent (5%) for ten (10) years."

In view of the foregoing, as a CFZ registered domestic market enterprise, Berthaphil is allowed to continue availing the preferential tax rate of 5%, in lieu of all local and national internal revenue taxes, for a period not exceeding ten (10) years from the effectivity of the CREATE Act. Thus, it is exempt from paying the regular income tax, and its lessees are not required to withhold the 5% creditable withholding tax on rental payments for the lease of Berthaphil's properties. CAIHTE

This ruling is issued on the basis of the facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be disclosed that the actual facts are different, then this ruling shall be without force and effect insofar as the herein parties are concerned.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Jesuit Communications Foundation, Inc.
Sonolux Bldg. Seminary Drive, Ateneo de Manila University
Loyola Heights, Quezon City 1108

Attention: AAA

_______________

This refers to your request to amend the Certificate of Tax Exemption of Jesuit Communications Foundation, Inc. (JesCom) to include tax exemption from income tax and value-added tax (VAT), and to issue revised Certificate of Registration (BIR Form No. 2303) to reflect the new coverage of the tax exemption.

It is represented that JesCom is a non-stock, non-profit corporation. It was organized primarily to provide support to the task of the Catholic Church in the Philippines and in other parts of Asia to integrate the faith and life of the faithful through any means of communications for evangelization and total human development. HTcADC

On December 16, 2022, the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), through Revenue Region No. 7A-Quezon City, has issued CTE No. 039-1022-0276-EXEMPT which provides among others that JesCom is exempt from income tax on the following revenues or receipts:

1. Proceeds from distribution of liturgical and inspirational music, religious books, videos, songbooks for liturgical music and other merchandize;

2. Proceeds from the use of sound studio, facilities, equipment and video production assistance;

3. Donation from media ethics training services offered to priests, nuns and lays;

4. Royalties from mechanical and synchronization, licenses, public performance, and print of the Foundation's religious music, television and radio shows; and

5. Other types of donations arising from fund-raising activities.

JesCom now seeks to be exempt not only from income tax but also from VAT on the above-mentioned revenues or receipts.

It is your considered position that the said sources of receipts are not only exempt from income tax but likewise from VAT. This position is anchored on the case of Association of Non-Profit Clubs, Inc. (ANPC) vs. BIR. [1] According to you, the Supreme Court articulated clearly the distinction between "capital" and "income." Similarly, the receipts and various sources of funds for JesCom are not for business but primarily intended for JesCom's general operation, activities and the entire communications infrastructure for evangelization and human development. As such, the said receipts cannot be classified as the income of JesCom from whatever source that are subject to income tax. The same only form part of capital from which no income tax may be collected or imposed.

You also mentioned that in the same case, the Supreme Court declared as invalid the BIR's interpretation that membership fee, association dues, and the like are part of the gross receipts of recreational clubs that are subject to VAT. In equal footing, you posit that the receipts of JesCom are likewise not subject to VAT as there is no sale, barter or exchange of commercial goods or services. Moreover, JesCom being a non-stock, non-profit religious institution is among the entities covered by Section 30 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997 (Tax Code), as amended, and therefore is at a different and higher level than recreational clubs because they are excluded under said section.

In reply, please be informed that Section 105 of the Tax Code, as amended, provides that:

"SEC. 105. Persons Liable. — Any person who, in the course of trade or business, sells, barters, exchanges, leases goods or properties, renders services, and any person who imports goods shall be subject to the value-added tax (VAT) imposed in Sections 106 to 108 of this Code.

The value-added tax is an indirect tax and the amount of tax may be shifted or passed on to the buyer, transferee or lessee of the goods, properties or services. This rule shall likewise apply to existing contracts of sale or lease of goods, properties or services at the time of the effectivity of Republic Act No. 7716.

The phrase 'in the course of trade or business' means the regular conduct or pursuit of a commercial or an economic activity, including transactions incidental thereto, by any person regardless of whether or not the person engaged therein is a non-stock, nonprofit private organization (irrespective of the disposition of its net income and whether or not it sells exclusively to members or their guests), or government entity.

xxx xxx xxx"

(Emphasis and underscoring supplied)

The provision clarifies that even a non-stock, non-profit organization, among others, is liable to pay VAT on the sale of goods or services. VAT is a tax on transactions, imposed at every stage of the distribution process on the sale, barter, exchange of goods or property, and on the performance of services, even in the absence of profit attributable thereto. The term "in the course of trade or business" requires the regular conduct or pursuit of a commercial or an economic activity regardless of whether the entity is profit-oriented.

The definition of the term "in the course of trade or business" applies to all transactions. Any person who, in the course of trade or business, sells, barters or exchanges goods and services, is liable to pay VAT. It likewise stresses that even a non-stock, non-profit organization or government entity is liable to pay VAT for the sale of goods and services. CAIHTE

Section 108 of the Tax Code, as amended, defines the phrase "sale of service" as the performance of all kinds of services for others for a fee, remuneration or consideration. It is immaterial whether the primary purpose of JesCom's general operation, activities and the entire communications infrastructure for evangelization and human development is not for realizing profit, for purposes of determining liability for VAT on services rendered. As long as the entity provides service for a fee, remuneration or consideration, then the service rendered is subject to VAT.

At any rate, it is a rule that because taxes are the lifeblood of the nation, statutes that allow exemptions are construed strictly against the grantee and liberally in favor of the government. Otherwise stated, any exemption from the payment of a tax must be clearly stated in the language of the law; it cannot be merely implied therefrom. In the case of VAT, Section 109 of the Tax Code, as amended, clearly enumerates the transactions exempted from VAT. The services rendered by JesCom do not fall within the exemptions.

It is worth noting that the Supreme Court, in the case of ANPC vs. BIR, stated that:

"Membership fees, assessment dues, and the like are not subject to VAT because in collecting such fees, the club is not selling its service to the members. Conversely, the members are not buying services from the club when dues are paid; hence, there is no economic or commercial activity to speak of as these dues are devoted for the operations/maintenance of the facilities of the organization. As such, there could be no 'sale, barter or exchange of goods or properties, or sale of a service' to speak of, which would then be subject to VAT under the 1997 NIRC." (Emphasis supplied)

The foregoing however does not apply to JesCom due to the clear difference between the transactions. It does not receive payment for the maintenance and operations of its facilities but instead for the services it offers.

The difference essentially lies in the way the transactions are structured. In the case of ANPC, it receives membership dues from its members solely for the purpose of the upkeep of the club facilities. Club members pay not for the privilege of using the club's facilities but for their maintenance. JesCom receives payments from its customers for the privilege of using its liturgical and inspirational music, religious books, videos, songbooks for liturgical music and other merchandise; sound studio, facilities, equipment and video production assistance; media ethics training services offered to priests, nuns, and lays; mechanical synchronization licenses, public performance, and print of the Foundations' religious music, television and radio shows; and video and audio equipment and instruments, and other communications and studio room and facilities, which is basically a sale of service contemplated under Section 108 of the Tax Code, as amended.

In the same vein, JesCom cited the discussion on income as distinguished from capital, to wit:

"Income as contrasted with capital or property is to be the test. The essential difference between capital and income is that capital is a fund; income is a flow. A fund of property existing at an instant of time is called capital. A flow of services rendered by that capital by the payment of money from it or any other benefit rendered by a fund of capital in relation to such fund through a period of time is called income. Capital is wealth, while income is the service of wealth.

xxx xxx xxx

As correctly argued by ANPC, membership fees, assessment dues, and other fees of similar nature only constitute contributions to and/or replenishment of the funds for the maintenance and operations of the facilities offered by recreational clubs to their exclusive members. They represent funds 'held in trust' by these clubs to defray their operating and general costs and hence, only constitute infusion of capital." (Emphasis and underscoring supplied)

In the case of JesCom, their receipts are considered income and not capital. The amount they receive is from a flow of services rendered by capital. Their capital is their liturgical and inspirational music, religious books, videos, songbooks for liturgical music and other merchandise; sound studio, facilities, equipment and video production assistance; media ethics training services offered to priests, nuns, and lays; mechanical synchronization licenses, public performance, and print of the Foundations' religious music, television and radio shows; and video and audio equipment, and instruments, and other communications and studio room and facilities, for which they get paid for. By selling the right to use their properties, their capital serves to acquire income. This is opposed to membership fees, assessment dues, and other fees of similar nature since, by their very nature, they are contributions only and are treated as funds held in trust by clubs. Meanwhile, the funds JesCom collects are not held in trust for members but are theirs solely, which they can dispose of in any manner whatsoever. Only in this particular case, they decided to utilize it to provide support to the task of the Catholic Church in the Philippines and in other parts of Asia to integrate the faith and life of the faithful through any means of communications for evangelization and total human development. Simply doing this, however, does not automatically convert JesCom's income to capital. aScITE

Please be guided accordingly.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Thus, the transfer of the legal title of the MPCI share from the former Trustee-appointee to the new Trustee-appointee is not subject to CGT under Section 24 (C) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997 (Tax Code),as amended, considering that the transfer involves neither monetary consideration nor change in beneficial ownership. Clearly, there is no intention on the part of SCB to donate to the new Trustee-appointee the MPCI share since the transaction is purely for a legitimate business purpose. Thus, the transfer will not be subject to donor's tax since there is no intention to donate, and the transaction is a bona fide transaction effected solely for business reasons.

The transfer is not subject to DST.

The transfer is not subject to DST under Section 175 of the Tax Code, as amended. The rule in this jurisdiction is that the assignment of shares of stock of a domestic corporation is subject to DST upon execution of the deed transferring ownership or rights thereto, or upon delivery, assignment or indorsement of such shares in favor of another.

Section 4 thereof provides:

"For a sale or exchange to be taxable, there must be an actual or constructive transfer of beneficial ownership of the shares of stock from one person to another. Such transfer may be manifested by the clear exercise of attributes of ownership over such stocks by the transferee, or by an actual entry of a change in the name appearing in the certificate of stock or in the Stock and Transfer Book of the issuing corporation or by any entry indicating transfer of beneficial ownership in any form of registry including those of a duly authorized scripless registry, such as those maintained for or by the Philippine Stock Exchange. However, if by the transfer of certificates of stock from a resigned trustee to a newly appointed trustee such certificate of stock remain in the name of the cestui que trust or the resigned trustee so that the new trustee is constituted as mere depository of the stock, such transfer is not taxable. Provided, however, that transfer of shares to 'nominees' to qualify them to sit in the board or to qualify them to perform any act in relation to the corporation shall not be subject to the DST provided herein only upon proof of a duly executed Nominee Agreement showing the purpose of the transfer; that the transfer is without consideration other than the undertaking of the nominee to only represent the beneficial owner of the stock; and the transfer is in trust." (Underscoring supplied.)

Therefore, the herein transfer cannot be subject to DST as there is no transfer or conveyance to the new trustee of the beneficial ownership of any right, claim or interest over the MPCI share or over the asset of MPCI. There being no new conveyance to speak of in this case, there is no new exercise of a privilege upon which DST may be imposed. aScITE

However, the notarial acknowledgment to the Deed of Declaration of Trust is subject to DST imposed under Section 188 of the Tax Code, as amended.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be ascertained that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request on behalf of TeaM (Philippines) Energy Corporation ("TPEC"),for confirmation that the assignment by TPEC to the Japanese Government of its carbon credits, in the form of Joint Crediting Mechanism ("JCM") Program credits, from the operation of its Mariwasa-Siam Ceramics, Inc. Solar Power Rooftop Power Plant Project ("Project"), in exchange for cash received from the Japanese Government, constitutes a sale of carbon emission credit. Hence, the proceeds of which are exempt from any and all taxes pursuant to Section 15 (i) of Republic Act ("RA") No. 9513. [1] HTcADC

Background:

1. TPEC (Taxpayer Identification Number: 000-000-000-00000) is a domestic corporation engaged in the business of, among others, developing, designing, constructing, erecting, assembling, commissioning, owning, operating, maintaining, rehabilitating and managing facilities used in the generation of electricity, including but not limited to gas-turbine and other power generating plants and related facilities.

2. TPEC is registered with the Department of Energy as a Renewable Energy ("RE") Developer of the Project located in Brgy. San Antonio, Sto. Tomas, Batangas, under Certificate of Registration No. SEOC 2023-10-719 dated November 21, 2023.

3. TPEC is registered with the Board of Investments ("BOI") as an RE Developer of Solar Energy Resources, including TPEC's 3.146 MWp/2.600 MWac Mariwasa-Siam Ceramics, Inc. Solar Power Rooftop Project, with BOI Certificate of Registration No. 2024-085 dated April 15, 2024.

4. Marubeni Corporation ("MC") is an entity duly organized and existing under the laws of Japan with address at 4-2, Ohtemachi 1-chome, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, Japan.

5. TPEC and MC (the Japanese participant) entered into an agreement, which took effect on July 26, 2022, to: (a) establish an international consortium called "Consortium for Energy Supply Project by 9MW Solar Power System to Ceramic Factory and Cement Plant" and (b) utilize the financial programme for the project on carbon dioxide emission reductions as "The Joint Crediting Mechanism Model Project 2022" (the "Agreement").

6. The JCM program, subject of the Agreement, is a bilateral economic collaboration between Japan and its partner country (in this case, the Philippines) that focuses on the tracking of carbon credits as the quantitative evidence of greenhouse gas ("GHG") emission reductions or removals. These carbon credits, also called "JCM credits," would be acquired by the Japanese Government to achieve Japan's GHG emission reduction target under the Kyoto Protocol.

7. The Project utilizes a technology that allows it to generate electricity without producing GHG, hence, was registered with the JCM program of the Japanese Government through Ministry of Environment in Japan ("MOEJ").

8. Under the Agreement, and in relation to the JCM Guidelines, the Japanese Government, acting through the MOEJ, provides funding for the construction of the Project (through MC).In consideration of this funding, the Consortium, of which TPEC is part of, will transfer the JCM credits that will be generated from the GHG emission achieved through the Project and assign to the Japanese Government. The MOEJ will determine the percentage of JCM credits that will be transferred to the Japanese Government. [2]

In reply, please be informed that Section 15 (i) of RA No. 9513 provides that the proceeds from the sale of carbon emission credits are exempt from any and all taxes, including, but not limited to, income tax and value-added tax ("VAT"),to wit:

"Section 15. Incentives for Renewable Energy Projects and Activities. — RE Developers of renewable energy facilities, including hybrid systems, in proportion to and to the extent of the RE component, for both power and non-power applications, as duly certified by the DOE, in consultation with the BOI, shall be entitled to the following incentives:

xxx xxx xxx

(i) Tax Exemption of Carbon Credits — All proceeds from the sale of carbon emission credits shall be exempt from any and all taxes." (Underscoring supplied)

The above fiscal incentive is also stated in Section 4 (F) of Revenue Regulations ("RR") No. 7-2022, [3] which was issued by the Bureau of Internal Revenue ("BIR") to institutionalize the tax incentive provisions of RA No. 9513.

Therefore, applied in this case, all proceeds from sale of carbon credits by TPEC is exempt from all taxes, provided, that it complies with the conditions stated under RA No. 9513 and RR No. 7-2022. CAIHTE

Article 1458 of the Civil Code of the Philippines provides that by a contract of sale, "one of the contracting parties obligates himself to transfer the ownership and to deliver a determinate thing, and the other to pay thereof a price certain in money or its equivalent." Hence, the requisites of a valid contract of sale are: (1) consent or meeting of the minds; (2) determinate subject matter; and (3) price certain in money or its equivalent. [4] In a contract of sale, its perfection is consummated at the moment there is a meeting of the minds upon the thing that is the object of the contract and upon the price. Consent is manifested by the meeting of the offer and the acceptance of the thing and the cause, which are to constitute the contract. [5]

A perusal of the Agreement shows that the elements of a contract of sale are present in the case at bar. First,by signing the Agreement, the parties indicate their consent to all the rights and obligations outlined therein, including the transfer of ownership of the carbon credits to the Japanese Government for a price. Second,the determinate subject matter is JCM credits generated from Project power plant's operations. Lastly,the funding to be made (or the consideration to be paid) by the Japanese Government is equivalent to the costs that can be verified as having been spent for implementation of the Project. Hence, there is a "price certain in money" involved in the transaction. Clearly the transaction envisioned under the Agreement is a sale of carbon credits.

Moreover, the Project is in line with the Memorandum of Cooperation between Japan and the Republic of the Philippines on Low Carbon Growth Partnership dated January 12, 2017, and the JCM credits are in accordance with the JCM guidelines promulgated thereunder. The primary objective of such Memorandum is to promote investment and the use of technologies, products, systems, services and infrastructure in order to achieve low carbon growth in the Philippines based on the principles of equality, reciprocity and mutual benefit, in accordance with their respective domestic laws, regulations and environmental policies as well as their budget availability.

Having all these in regard, for tax purposes, the subject transaction partakes the nature of a sale, as contemplated under RA No. 9513 and RR No. 7-2022. It is a settled principle that equity and law always exalt substance over form. It is the nature of the instrument which will determine whether there is a sale or not and not the particular label or nomenclature of the document which embody them. [6] Simply put, the taxability of transactions or agreements depends on their substance which is paramount over their forms.

Such being the case, this Office hereby rules that the delivery of carbon emission credits under the JCM program by TPEC to the Japanese Government is actually a sale. Hence, the proceeds received by TPEC relating to such sale (or the funding received from the Japanese Government) is exempt from any and all taxes, including, but not limited to income tax and VAT, under the existing laws, rules and regulations. aScITE

This ruling is issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation it shall be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) FAITH M. FAROCHILEN-UMANDAP
OIC-Assistant Commissioner

Gentlemen :

This refers to your letter on behalf of Presidential Commission on Good Government ("PCGG") requesting for a confirmatory ruling that the transfer of Coco Levy Assets, particularly the 2,763,633 shares of stock in Top Frontier Investment Holdings, Inc. ("TFIHI") registered under the PCGG in Trust for the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program ("PCGG in Trust for CARP") to the Republic of the Philippines ("ROP") is exempt from stock transfer tax and other related taxes.

Background:

1. PCGG is the registered owner of 27,636,339 shares of stock of San Miguel Corporation ("SMC") in the name of "PCGG in Trust for CARP."

2. The Board of Directors of SMC declared as property dividends its shareholdings in TFIHI in favor of the registered SMC common stockholders as of November 5, 2013, making all common shareholders of SMC entitled to receive one (1) TFIHI common share for every ten (10) SMC common shares. The PCGG received 2,763,633 TFIHI common shares registered in the name of PCGG in Trust for CARP (the "Shares").

3. The PCGG and the Bureau of Treasury executed a Deed of Assignment and Transfer of Title on January 16, 2024 for the transfer to the ROP the Shares. In this regard, your Office is to apply for the issuance of eCAR (Certificate Authorizing Registration) by the Bureau of Internal Revenue to facilitate the issuance of new stock certificates in the name of ROP.

In reply, please be informed as follows:

Capital Gains Tax

Relevant provisions of Republic Act ("RA") No. 11524 states:

"IV
Reconveyance of Coconut Levy Assets and/or Funds

SECTION 6. Reconveyance. — Within one (1) year upon the effectivity of this Act, all government agencies, except the BTr, and any person having any Coconut Levy Asset and/or Fund in its administration, authority, custody, or control which have been finally declared by the Supreme Court as belonging to the government, shall perform or cause the performance of the following:

(1) Reconvey title to the Republic of the Philippines;

(2) Deliver all stock certificates and other evidence of ownership to the BTr for safekeeping; and

(3) Transfer all cash Coconut Levy Assets to the Trust Fund.

They shall likewise perform or cause the performance of the aforementioned acts on Coconut Levy Assets that may hereafter be recovered as belonging to the government to the benefit of the coconut farmers and the development of the coconut industry.

No temporary restraining order (TRO) or any injunction order can be issued on the aforementioned acts except by the Supreme Court.

xxx xxx xxx

V
Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund

SECTION 7. The Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund. — There is hereby created a Trust Fund to be known as the "Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund," referred to in this Act as the "Trust Fund," which shall be capitalized, managed, invested, utilized and accounted for in the manner provided in this Act.

xxx xxx xxx

The Trust Fund shall thereafter be augmented with all proceeds of privatization or disposition of the Coconut Levy Assets remitted directly thereto by the BTr, Privatization and Management Office (PMO), or other DDEs in accordance with this Act, including any and all forms of income, interests, earnings, yields, or any monetary benefit derived prior to the privatization or disposition of any of the Coconut Levy Assets, and any and all forms of income, interests, earnings, yields, or any monetary benefits derived from retained Coconut Levy Assets. All Coconut Levy Assets in the name of the Philippine Government shall be sold within the period of five (5) years after the effectivity of this Act, and all other Coconut Levy Assets that may hereafter be recovered shall likewise be disposed of within five (5) years from the time it is declared as belonging to the government, and the proceeds shall be transferred to the Trust Fund for the benefit of the coconut farmers.

xxx xxx xxx

VI
Disposition of Non-Cash Coconut Levy Assets

SECTION 13. Disposition of Non-Cash Coconut Levy Assets. — Coconut Levy Assets defined in Section 3 hereof, which are assigned by the Trust Fund Management Committee to DDEs shall be privatized or disposed subject to the regulatory approvals as required by law within the period of five (5) years from the effectivity of this Act.

This Act shall in no case exempt Coconut Levy Assets from the respective jurisdictions of the various applicable regulators, particularly the Governance Commission for Government-owned or -controlled corporations (GCG), the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation (PDIC), and the Insurance Commission (IC)." (Underscoring supplied)

Based on the afore-quoted provisions, it is evident that it is imperative that Coconut Levy Assets, such as the Shares be transferred to the ROP.

Section 27 (D) (2) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended ("Tax Code"), provides that a final tax at the rate of fifteen percent (15%) shall be imposed on net capital gains realized during the taxable year from the sale, exchange or other disposition of shares of stock in a domestic corporation except shares sold or disposed of through the stock exchange.

While the transfer or disposition of Shares appears to fall under Section 27 (D) (2) of the Tax Code, please note that the said transfer is pursuant to the directive under Section 6 of RA No. 11524. In BIR Ruling No. OT-422-2022, this Office ruled, among others, that since the transfer of shares was made in compliance with the directive under RA No. 11524, the same shall not be subject to internal revenue taxes.

Such being the case, this Office hereby rules that the transfer or disposition of Shares (as contemplated under RA No. 11524) is not subject to capital gains tax.

Donor's Tax

Section 98 of the Tax Code provides that donor's tax shall be imposed upon the transfer by any person, resident or nonresident, of a property by gift or donation. Article 725 of the New Civil Code of the Philippines defines donation as "an act of liberality whereby a person disposes gratuitously of a thing or right in favor of another, who accepts it." Hence, to be a valid donation, it is essential that: (1) there is reduction of the patrimony of the donor; (2) there is increase in the patrimony of the donee; (3) the intent on the part of the donor to do an act of liberality (animus donandi); and (4) the donee accepts the gift.

Evaluating the facts of this case shows that, in transferring the Shares to ROP, there was no donative intent on the part of PCGG but the same was pursued solely to comply with Section 6 of RA No. 11524.

Thus, the transfer of Shares to ROP shall not be subject to donor's tax.

Documentary Stamp Tax

The transfer of Shares by PCGG to ROP is not subject to DST imposed under Section 175 of the Tax Code which provides that DST shall be imposed on all conveyances of shares in any corporation. Please note that there is no sale or delivery or transfer of shares of stocks as contemplated under Section 175 of the Tax Code. To reiterate, the transfer of shares of stocks of the Corporation to PCGG is made in order to comply with Section 6 of RA No. 11524.

Accordingly, this Office hereby rules that the transfer of Shares by PCGG to ROP is not subject to DST.

This ruling is issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation it shall be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Background:

1. On March 21, 1986, Mr. Jose Y. Campos surrendered to the Republic of the Philippines thru PCGG various companies including the Corporations.

2. The Corporations own the following equity in Chemfields, Inc.:

Corporation

3. Chemfields, Inc. is a holding company whose sole business interest is managing its investment in Center of Excellence in Drug Research, Evaluation and Studies, Inc.

4. Under Administrative Order ("AO") No. 231 dated August 23, 1991, as amended by AO No. 241 dated October 4, 1991, PCGG is mandated to privatize all assets it recovered including those turned over by Jose Y. Campos.

5. On February 10, 2023, the Corporations approved the transfer to the Republic of the Philippines thru PCGG their respective shareholdings in Chemfields, Inc. Deeds of Assignment were executed by the Corporations to implement the said transfer.

In reply, please be informed as follows:

CGT

Section 27 (D) (2) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended ("Tax Code"), provides that gains derived by a domestic corporation from the sale, exchange or other disposition of shares of stock not traded in the stock exchange shall be subject to fifteen percent (15%) final income tax, to wit:

"SEC. 27. Rates of Income Tax on Domestic Corporations. —

xxx xxx xxx

(D) Rates of Tax on Certain Passive Incomes. —

xxx xxx xxx

(2) Capital Gains from the Sale of Shares of Stock Not Traded in the Stock Exchange — A final tax at the rate of fifteen percent (15%) shall be imposed on net capital gains realized during the taxable year from the sale, exchange or other disposition of shares of stock in a domestic corporation except shares sold or disposed of through the stock exchange." (Emphasis and underscoring supplied)

The foregoing provision does not apply to the instant case. Pursuant to AO No. 241, PCGG has the control and disposal responsibility over the assets, shares of stocks, and such other properties recovered from, turned over by, or pertaining to, Mr. Jose Y. Campos. In order to perform the obligations and functions of PCGG under AO Nos. 231 and 241, it is necessary to transfer the property/ies first to the National Government thru PCGG.

Consequently, since the transfer of shares of stock of the Corporations to the National Government thru PCGG is made in compliance with the directive under AO Nos. 231 and 241, there is no sale, barter or exchange of the shares of stock of the Corporations as contemplated in Section 27 (D) (2) of the Tax Code. [1]

Such being the case, this Office is of the position that the transfer of shares from the Corporations to PCGG is not subject to CGT.

Donor's Tax

Section 98 of the Tax Code provides that donor's tax shall be imposed upon the transfer by any person, resident or nonresident, of a property by gift or donation. Article 725 of the New Civil Code of the Philippines defines donation as "an act of liberality whereby a person disposes gratuitously of a thing or right in favor of another, who accepts it." Hence, to be a valid donation, it is essential that: (1) there is reduction of the patrimony of the donor; (2) there is increase in the patrimony of the donee; (3) the intent on the part of the donor to do an act of liberality (animus donandi); and (4) the donee accepts the gift.

Evaluating the facts of this case shows that, in transferring the shares of the stocks of the Corporations to PCGG, there was no donative intent on the part of Corporations but the same was pursued solely to comply with AO Nos. 231 and 241.

Thus, the transfer of shares of stocks of the Corporations to PCGG shall not be subject to donor's tax.

DST

The transfer of shares of stocks of the Corporations to PCGG is not subject to DST imposed under Section 196 of the Tax Code which provides that DST shall be imposed on all conveyances, donations of real properties. Please note that there is no sale or delivery or transfer of shares of stocks as contemplated under Section 196 of the Tax Code. To reiterate, the transfer of shares of stocks of the Corporation to PCGG is made in order to comply with the directive of AO Nos. 231 and 241.

Accordingly, this Office hereby rules that the transfer of shares of stocks of the Corporations to PCGG is not subject to DST.

This ruling is issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation it shall be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.

Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Details.Details:
Sections 24 (D) (1), 188, and 196 of the NIRC of 1997,
as amended; BIR Ruling No. OT-0371-2020

Mawis Law Office
Room 223, 2/F COMFOODS Building, Gil Puyat
cor. Chino Roces Avenue, San Antonio, Makati City, 1200

Attention: AAA

Gentlemen :

This refers to your letter requesting for confirmation, on behalf of the Atlantic Knitting Mills Corporation ("Atlantic"), that the reconveyance of two (2) parcels of land with improvements thereon, situated at 50 San Francisco St., Barangay Karuhatan, Valenzuela City, is not subject to Capital Gains Tax (CGT) and Documentary Stamp Tax (DST), pursuant to a Decision of the Metropolitan Trial Court (MeTC) Branch 82 in the City of Valenzuela. SDAaTC

It is represented that Atlantic is a corporation duly organized and constituted in accordance with Philippine laws and duly registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission with Registration Number 68773 and Tax Identification Number 000-000-000-00000. Atlantic's principal office address is at 50 San Francisco St., Barangay Karuhatan, Valenzuela City.

Background

1. Sometime in 1976, BBB ("BBB"), then a member of Atlantic's Board of Directors, purchased two (2) parcels of land with improvements thereon located at 50 San Francisco St., Barangay Karuhatan, Valenzuela City for the benefits and use of Atlantic.

2. BBB purchased the said properties using the funds provided by Atlantic. The purchased properties were registered with the Register of Deeds of Valenzuela City under the name of BBB as stated in Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) No. B-1321 and TCT No. B-1192.

3. During the entirety of BBB's tenure as a member of the Board of Directors, he was never in the possession of the said properties nor exercised acts of dominion over the same. In contrast, Atlantic has been in open, continuous, exclusive, and notorious possession of the said properties during the same period. As such, the subject properties were continuously occupied and used by Atlantic in its business operations.

4. The Owner's Duplicate Copy of the TCTs of the subject properties remained in the possession of Atlantic's founder, CCC. Moreover, Atlantic was up to date on its payment of real property taxes due thereon. AaCTcI

5. Upon the death of CCC, DDD ("DDD") served as Atlantic's President. During his incumbency, DDD discovered that the subject properties were registered under the name of BBB instead of Atlantic. BBB honestly believed that the TCTs were registered under the name of Atlantic.

6. On February 6, 2020, BBB executed an Affidavit of Existence of Trust, which was thereafter annotated at the back of the aforementioned TCTs on March 12, 2020. In the said Affidavit, BBB affirmed that the subject properties were acquired on behalf of and by using the funds of Atlantic.

7. Thereafter, Atlantic filed a Petition for Reconveyance, Cancellation Title, and Issuance of New Title before MeTC Branch 82 in the City of Valenzuela which was docketed as Civil Case No. 10824.

8. In the said Civil Case, BBB filed his Answer wherein he categorically admitted that he voluntarily executed the Affidavit of Existence of Trust and confirmed the facts stated therein in relation to the acquisition, occupation, and possession of the subject properties. He asserted that he does not claim ownership over the same.

9. On February 8, 2022, the MeTC Branch 82 in the City of Valenzuela rendered a Decision as follows:

"WHEREFORE, premises considered, judgment is hereby rendered as follows:

(1) Declaring the existence of implied resulting trust between BBB, as trustee, and Atlantic Knitting Mills Corporation, as beneficiary, over the properties covered by TCT No. B-1321 and TCT No. B-1192;

(2) Ordering BBB to transfer or reconvey the properties covered by TCT No. B-1321 and TCT No. B-1192 to Atlantic Knitting Mills Corporation; and

(3) Ordering the Register of Deeds of Valenzuela City to cancel TCT No. B-1321 and TCT No. B-1192, both under the name of BBB, and in lieu thereof to issue new certificates of title in the name of Atlantic Knitting Mills Corporation.

SO ORDERED."

10. On September 20, 2022, the MeTC Branch 82 in the City of Valenzuela issued a Certificate of Finality indicating that no appeal has been made by the concerned parties despite receipt of the aforementioned Decision and hence the decision became FINAL and EXECUTORY. acEHCD

11. In accordance with the abovementioned MeTC Decision, BBB executed a Deed of Reconveyance on January 20, 2023 wherein the parcels of land, described in TCT No. B-1321 and TCT No. B-1192, were assigned, transferred, and reconveyed from BBB to Atlantic.

12. Atlantic seeks exemption from the imposition of CGT and DST as the reconveyance of the subject properties pursuant to the MeTC Decision is without consideration and was done to return the properties to its rightful owner.

Hence, this request.

In reply, please be informed as follows:

Section 24 (D) (1) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended ("Tax Code"), imposes a final tax of six percent (6%) upon the capital gains presumed to have been realized from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of real property located in the Philippines. The said 6% CGT is computed on the basis of the gross selling price or current fair market value, whichever is higher. Section 24 (D) (1) reads:

"Section 24. Income Tax Rates. —

xxx xxx xxx

(D) Capital Gains from Sale of Real Property. —

(1) In General. — The provisions of Section 39(B) notwithstanding, a final tax of six percent (6%) based on the gross selling price or current fair market value as determined in accordance with Section 6(E) of this Code, whichever is higher, is hereby imposed upon capital gains presumed to have been realized from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of real property located in the Philippines, classified as capital assets, including pacto de retro sales and other forms of conditional sales, by individuals, including estates and trusts: Provided, That the tax liability, if any, on gains from sales or other dispositions of real property to the government or any of its political subdivisions or agencies or to government-owned or -controlled corporations shall be determined either under Section 24(A) or under this Subsection, at the option of the taxpayer." (Emphasis supplied)

In applying the foregoing, the imposition of CGT is based on the capital gains presumed to have been realized from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of real property. However, in this case, the reconveyance of the subject properties by virtue of the Decision of MeTC Branch 82 in the City of Valenzuela is without consideration, therefore no capital gains is presumed to have been realized. The reconveyance is for the purpose of returning the subject properties to the legal owners based upon the facts presented and the Affidavit of Existence of Trust. Hence, the transfer of the said properties from BBB to Atlantic, pursuant to a Court Decision, is not subject to CGT as imposed under Section 24 (D) (1) of the Tax Code. Consequently, the Deed of Reconveyance is also not subject to the DST imposed under Section 196 of the Tax Code. However, the notarial acknowledgement is subject to the Thirty pesos (P30.00) DST in accordance with Section 188 of the same Code. EcTCAD

The ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation it will be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Room 703, Erechem Building
Rufino cor. Salcedo St., San Lorenzo 1229
Makati City

Attention: AAA

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request on behalf of ACADEMIC PARADIGM, INC. for a value-added tax (VAT) exemption certificate pursuant to the provisions of Section 109 (1) (R) of the National Internal Revenue Code (Tax Code) of 1997, as amended.

It is represented that ACADEMIC PARADIGM, INC., with Taxpayer's Identification No. 000-000-000-000, is a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the Philippines; that it is duly registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) under SEC Reg. No. 2022110076114-03; and that it is engaged in the sale of, among others, e-journals, e-books, and other electronic materials used for educational purposes. HTcADC

In reply, please be informed that Section 109 (1) (R) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended, states that:

"Sec. 109. Exempt Transactions. —

(1) The following transactions shall be exempt from the value-added tax:

xxx xxx xxx

(R) Sale, importation, printing or publication of books and any newspaper, magazine, journal, review bulletin, or any such educational reading material covered by the UNESCO Agreement on the Importation of Educational, Scientific and Cultural Materials, including the digital or electronic format thereof: Provided, that the materials enumerated herein are not devoted principally to the publication of paid advertisements"

In view of the foregoing, this Office confirms that ACADEMIC PARADIGM, INC. is exempt from the twelve percent (12%) VAT on its sale of e-journals, e-books, and other electronic materials used for educational purposes, provided that such materials are not devoted principally to the publication of paid advertisements. CAIHTE

It is worth noting, however, that if ACADEMIC PARADIGM, INC. is engaged in other non-exempt activities such as the printing of brochures, bookbinding, engraving, stereotyping, electrotyping, lithographing of various reference books, trade books, journals and other literary works, said transactions are subject to VAT, and the taxpayer shall be required to register its business as VAT business entity and must issue a separate VAT invoice therefor to record the same.

It bears stressing that VAT is an indirect tax payable by the seller and not the purchaser of goods. Being an indirect tax, it can be shifted or passed on to the buyer/purchaser, transferee or lessee of the goods, properties or services. Once shifted to the buyer/customer as an addition to the cost of goods or services sold, it is no longer a tax but an additional cost which the buyer/customer has to pay in order to obtain the goods or services. Thus, the shifting of the VAT to ACADEMIC PARADIGM, INC. does not make it the person directly liable and therefore, it cannot invoke its tax exemption privilege under Section 109 (1) (R) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended, to avoid the passing on or shifting of the VAT. Hence, its purchase of goods, properties, or services from its suppliers shall nevertheless be subject to the 12% VAT pursuant to Section 106 of the same Code.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be ascertained that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered as null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request for confirmation that the tax exemptions of Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) pertaining to its gaming operations are extended to Playmate Leisure Solutions Corp. ("PLSC"), being a contractee and licensee, hence, PLSC's income from its gaming operations are likewise not subject to corporate income tax (CIT) and value-added tax (VAT) but only subject to 5% franchise tax pursuant to Section 13 (2) (a) and (b) of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1869, as amended. aScITE

Background

As represented, PLSC is a domestic corporation organized and existing under the laws of the Republic of the Philippines doing business under the name and style of Playmate Leisure Solutions Corp.

On October 24, 2023, PAGCOR gave PLSC, under Grant of Authority, the authority to hold and operate Electronic Games. The basis of authority of PAGCOR to issue the grant to PLSC is based on Sections 8 and 9 of PD No. 1869, as amended, which read as follows:

"Section 8. Registration. — All persons primarily engaged in gambling, together with their allied business, with contract or franchise from the Corporation shall register and affiliate their business with the Corporation. The Corporation shall issue the corresponding certificates of affiliation upon compliance by the registering entity with the promulgated rules and regulations thereon.

"Section 9. Regulatory Power. — The corporation shall maintain a Registry of the affiliated entities, and shall exercise all the powers, authority and the responsibilities vested in the Securities and Exchange Commission over such affiliated entities mentioned under the preceding section, including but not limited to amendments of Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws, change in corporate term, structure, capitalization and other matters concerning the operation of the affiliating entities, the provisions of the Corporation Code of the Philippines to the contrary notwithstanding, except only with respect to original incorporation."

Hence, this request. DETACa

Discussion/Ruling

In reply, please be informed that Section 13 (2) (a) and (b) of PD No. 1869, as amended by Republic Act (RA) No. 9487, provides:

"SEC. 13. Exemptions. —

(2) Income and other taxes — (a) Franchise Holder: No tax of any kind or form, income or otherwise, as well as fees, charges or levies of whatever nature, whether National or Local, shall be assessed and collected under this Franchise from the Corporation, nor shall any form of tax or charge attach in any way to the earnings of the Corporation, except a Franchise Tax of five (5%) percent of the gross revenue or earnings derived by the Corporation from its operation under this Franchise. Such tax shall be due and payable quarterly to the National Government and shall be in lieu of all kinds of taxes, levies, fees or assessments of any kind, nature or description, levied, established or collected by any municipal, provincial, or national government authority.

xxx xxx xxx

(b) Others: The exemption herein granted for earnings derived from the operations conducted under the franchise, specifically from the payment of any tax, income or otherwise, as well as any form of charges, fees or levies, shall inure to the benefit of and extend to corporation(s), association(s), agency(ies), or individual(s) with whom the Corporation or operator has any contractual relationship in connection with the operations of the casino(s) authorized to be conducted under this Franchise and to those receiving compensation or other remuneration from the Corporation or operator as a result of essential facilities furnished and/or technical services rendered to the Corporation or operator." (Emphasis and underscoring supplied)

Considering the above-cited provisions, the Supreme Court clarified in Bloomberry Resorts and Hotels, Inc. v. Bureau of Internal Revenue, [1] that PAGCOR's tax privilege of paying only a five percent (5%) Franchise Tax for income generated from its gaming operations (i.e., casinos and other related amusement places), in lieu of all other taxes, inures to the benefit of PAGCOR's licensees.

Moreover, in the case of Bloomberry Resorts and Hotels, Inc. vs. Bureau of Internal Revenue, the Supreme Court declared in no uncertain terms that like PAGCOR, its contractees and licensees remain exempted from the payment of corporate income tax and other taxes since Section 13 (2) of PD No. 1869, as amended, is clear that said exemption inures to their benefit, viz.:

"Simply then, in this case, we adhere to the principle that since the statute is clear and free from ambiguity, it must be given its literal meaning and applied without attempted interpretation. This is the plain meaning rule or verba legis, as expressed in the maxim index animi sermo or speech is the index of intention. HEITAD

Plainly, too, upon payment of the 5% franchise tax, petitioner's income from its gaming operations of gambling casinos, gaming clubs and other similar recreation or amusement places, and gaming pools, defined within the purview of the aforesaid section, is not subject to corporate income tax."

With regard to the VAT exemption of PLSC, Section 109 (1) (K) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997 (Tax Code), as amended, provides:

"SEC. 109. Exempt Transactions. — (1) Subject to the provisions of Subsection (2) hereof, the following transactions shall be exempt from the value-added tax:

xxx xxx xxx

(K) Transactions which are exempt under international agreements to which the Philippines is a signatory or under special laws, except those under Presidential Decree No. 529;" (Emphasis supplied)

Thus, PAGCOR and its contractees/licensees are exempt from the payment of VAT because PAGCOR's charter, PD No. 1869, is a special law that grants PAGCOR exemption from taxes and such exemptions extend or inure to the benefit of its licensees.

Premises considered, this Office hereby rules that since PLSC is a contractee/licensee of PAGCOR, the exemption from taxes, fees and charges enjoyed by PAGCOR is extended to PLSC pursuant to Section 13 (2) (b) of PD No. 1869, as amended. Thus, the income derived by PLSC solely from its gaming operations is subject only to the 5% Franchise Tax, and shall be exempt from CIT and VAT. Therefore, your opinion that as PAGCOR contractee/licensee, PLSC shall only pay 5% Franchise Tax in lieu of all taxes on income from gaming operations, i.e., electronic bingo, sports betting, electronic (eCasino) games is hereby CONFIRMED but only during the validity of its Certificate of Authority issued by PAGCOR on the specified gaming site. However, for the purpose of applying the 5% franchise tax, any income that may be realized by PLSC from unrelated services or services not falling under gaming operations, shall be subject to CIT and VAT.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be ascertained that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request for confirmation that the transfer of Manila Polo Club (MPC) share owned by GINEBRA SAN MIGUEL, INC. ("GSMI") from a former trustee, BBB ("BBB") to a new trustee, CCC ("CCC") is not subject to the payment of taxes, and a Certificate Authorizing Registration (CAR) is not necessary to effect the said transfer. HTcADC

Background

1. As represented, GSMI is a domestic corporation engaged in the manufacture and sale of alcoholic beverages, and all business activities incidental or related to carrying out these activities.

2. GSMI is the beneficial owner of a membership share with MPC evidenced by Proprietary Membership Certificate No. 6242 (the "Membership Share"), which is registered in the name of BBB, a Board Director for GSMI.

3. Pursuant to the Declaration of Trust executed by BBB, GSMI may designate another person it seems qualified to be the new holder of the Membership Share and it seeks to designate CCC as the new trustee for its Membership Share in MPC and to place the Membership Share in the name of CCC. In line with the impending transfer of share, CCC executed a Declaration of Trust on April 22, 2024 acknowledging that GSMI is the true and actual owner of the MPC share, and that CCC does not have any title, claim or interest whatsoever over said MPC share.

Discussion/Ruling

The transfer of MPC shares from the Transferor
to the Transferee is not subject to CGT.

A declaration of trust has been defined as an act by which a person acknowledges that the property, title to which he holds, is held by him for the use of another. [1] CAIHTE

In the Declaration of Trust, which the declarant/appointee executed, he acknowledged that the transfer did not give him any kind of right, claim, or interest whatsoever in the MPC share and that he is holding only the legal ownership of the same with the beneficial ownership pertaining to the Company. Here, the Trustor is the Company while the Trustee is the declarant/appointee.

In the case of Sime Darby Pilipinas, Inc. v. Mendoza, [2] Sime Darby acquired a Class "A" club share in Alabang Country Club (ACC) in 1987, but being a corporation which was expressly disallowed by ACC's By-Laws to acquire and register the club share under its name, registered the share under the name of respondent Mendoza, Sime Darby's sales manager at the time. The Supreme Court held that a trust arrangement existed between Sime Darby and Mendoza and while the share was bought by Sime Darby and placed under the name of Mendoza, the latter's title was only limited to the use and enjoyment of the club's facilities and privileges while employed with the company.

In the instant case, GSMI, the purchaser of the MPC share, intends to give its legal title to its Trustee-appointee, which entitles the Trustee-appointee only to the use and enjoyment of the club's facilities since under the Articles of Incorporation and By-laws of MPC only natural persons may become registered members. Thus, the transfer of the legal title of the MPC shares from the former Trustee-appointee to the new Trustee-appointee is not subject to CGT under Section 24 (C) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997 (Tax Code), as amended, considering that the transfer involves neither monetary consideration nor change in beneficial ownership.

The transfer is not subject to donor's tax.

Well-settled in our jurisprudence is the fact that the essential elements of a valid donation are: (1) the reduction of the patrimony of the donor; (2) the increase in the patrimony of the donee; and (3) the intent to do an act of liberality (animus donandi). [3]

Clearly, there is no intention on the part of GSMI to donate to the new Trustee-appointee the MPC share since the transaction is purely for a legitimate business purpose. Thus, the transfer will not be subject to donor's tax since there is no intention to donate, and the transaction is a bona fide transaction effected solely for business reasons.

The transfer is not subject to DST.

The transfer is not subject to DST under Section 175 of the Tax Code, as amended. The rule in this jurisdiction is that the assignment of shares of stock of a domestic corporation is subject to DST upon execution of the deed transferring ownership or rights thereto, or upon delivery, assignment or indorsement of such shares in favor of another. aScITE

Revenue Regulations No. 13-2004, implementing the provisions of Republic Act No. 9243, otherwise known as "An Act Rationalizing the Provisions on the Documentary Stamp Tax of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, and for Other Purposes" qualified this rule by stating that for a sale or exchange to be taxable, there must be an actual or constructive transfer of beneficial ownership of the shares of stock from one person to another. Section 4 thereof provides:

"For a sale or exchange to be taxable, there must be an actual or constructive transfer of beneficial ownership of the shares of stock from one person to another. Such transfer may be manifested by the clear exercise of attributes of ownership over such stocks by the transferee, or by an actual entry of a change in the name appearing in the certificate of stock or in the Stock and Transfer Book of the issuing corporation or by any entry indicating transfer of beneficial ownership in any form of registry including those of a duly authorized scripless registry, such as those maintained for or by the Philippine Stock Exchange. However, if by the transfer of certificates of stock from a resigned trustee to a newly appointed trustee such certificate of stock remain in the name of the cestui que trust or the resigned trustee so that the new trustee is constituted as mere depository of the stock, such transfer is not taxable. Provided, however, that transfer of shares to 'nominees' to qualify them to sit in the board or to qualify them to perform any act in relation to the corporation shall not be subject to the DST provided herein only upon proof of a duly executed Nominee Agreement showing the purpose of the transfer; that the transfer is without consideration other than the undertaking of the nominee to only represent the beneficial owner of the stock; and the transfer is in trust." (Underscoring supplied.)

Therefore, the herein transfer cannot be subject to DST as there is no transfer or conveyance to the new trustee of the beneficial ownership of any right, claim or interest over the MPC share or over the asset of MPC. There being no new conveyance to speak of in this case, there is no new exercise of a privilege upon which DST may be imposed.

However, the notarial acknowledgment to the Deed of Declaration of Trust is subject to DST imposed under Section 188 of the Tax Code, as amended.

Finally, there is no need to secure a Tax Clearance (TCL) and/or Certificate Authorizing Registration (CAR) to effect the transfer of the MPC share in the name of the new trustee, CCC.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be ascertained that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void. DETACa

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue
