This refers to your request on behalf of Bank of the Philippine Islands ("BPI") for confirmation of the following opinion relating to the merger of BPI and BPI Family Savings Bank Incorporated ("BFSBI") with respect to the BPI Group of Companies Retirement Plan ("Retirement Plan"): DETACa

1. The length of service of BFSBI employees with BFSBI shall be considered for purposes of the ten (10)-year tenure requirement under the Retirement Plan; and

2. The merger does not affect the following tax benefits enjoyed under the Retirement Plan:

a. Retirement benefits to be received by the BFSBI employee-members shall be exempt from income tax;

b. The income of the Retirement Plan Trust Fund ("Retirement Fund") from its investments is exempt from income tax; and

c. BPI may deduct contributions to the Retirement Fund pursuant to Section 118 of the Income Tax Regulations or Revenue Regulations No. 2-1940, provided that the conditions set forth in the same are complied with.

Background

1. BPI is a commercial banking and trust corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the Philippines and duly licensed by the Central Bank of the Philippines (now Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas) as a universal bank.

2. BPI Group of Companies (which, for this purpose, include BFSBI) [1] established the Retirement Plan and a Certificate of Qualification as Reasonable Employee's Retirement Benefit Plan ("Certificate of Qualification") was issued by the Bureau of Internal Revenue in favor of the BPI Group of Companies on July 22, 2020, with the following tax incentives:

a. The retirement benefits to be received by the qualified employee-member shall be exempt from income tax provided that the two (2) conditions set forth under Section 32 (13) (6) (a) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended ("Tax Code") are satisfied: (i) the employee had been in the service of the same company for at least ten (10) years; and (ii) he is at least fifty (50) years old at the time of retirement;

b. The income of the Retirement Fund from its investments is exempt from income tax; and

c. The contributions of the company to the Retirement Fund are deductible from its gross income.

3. In 2020, BPI and BFSBI entered into a merger, with BPI as the surviving corporation and BFSBI as the absorbed corporation ("Merger"), which was approved by the Securities and Exchange Commission on December 21, 2022. [2] aScITE

4. The Merger became effective on January 1, 2022 [3] and consequently, all employees of BFSBI were absorbed by BPI.

In reply, please be informed as follows:

The length of service of BFSBI
employees with BFSBI shall be
considered for purposes of the ten
(10)-year tenure requirement under
the Retirement Plan

The Certificate of Qualification provides that BPI Group of Companies is entitled to tax incentives provided that it complies with the Terms and Conditions indicated therein. Section 2 of the said Terms and Conditions states that if the Retirement Plan allows portability of service credits, the benefits payable to the retiring member shall only be exempt from income tax when: (i) the employee had been in the service of the same company for at least ten (10) years; and (ii) he is at least fifty (50) years old at the time of retirement, to wit:

"TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THIS CERTIFICATE OF QUALIFICATION

xxx xxx xxx

(2) If the Retirement Plan allows portability of service credits, that is, a member transferring from the service of the Company to another participating company/affiliate company is allowed to carry his membership and retirement credits to the transferee company, the benefits payable to the retiring member shall only be exempt from income tax when the two (2) conditions under Section 32 (B) (6) (a) of the 1997 Tax Code, as amended are both present. In counting the ten (10)-year service requirement, only the length of service rendered for the past employer shall be considered, and those service years rendered for the past employer shall be disregarded. It is in consonance with the above requirement that the employee must have been in the service of the "same" employer for at least ten (10) years. For this purpose, the Company and other participating/affiliated companies, if any, are considered different employers." (Underscoring supplied)

Based on the above-cited provision, it is clear that the ten (10)-year service requirement would be counted only for the last employer and/or participating company.

It must be clarified however, that in case of transfer of employees from one participating company to another participating company within the multi-employer plan due to a valid merger or consolidation or for any other cause beyond the control of such employees, the aggregate years of service in the said companies shall be considered in computing the prescribed ten (10)-year period, provided, that said employees did not receive their respective separation pay from their previous employer/company (the absorbed or acquired company). [4]

Please note that in case of a merger, the surviving corporation has the legal obligation to assume all the obligations and liabilities of the absorbed corporation, including, for the avoidance of doubt, the employment contracts to preserve the constitutional and legal right of employees to security of tenure. [5]

In this case, as a consequence of the Merger, BPI, as the surviving corporation, has to absorb BFSBI's operations and all its assets and liabilities upon BFSBI's dissolution, including, for this purpose, its employees without prejudice to the right of BFSBI's employees to discontinue their services pursuant to prohibition against involuntary servitude. CAIHTE

Based on the above disquisitions, since the said transfer of employees is outside the control of the concerned employees, it is but just and fair to consider the period of service in both companies. [6]

Considering the foregoing, and considering further that the beneficial interests of the employees are of paramount importance especially in instances affecting their security of tenure due to cases beyond their control, this Office hereby rules that the length of service rendered to BFSBI by BFSBI employees who chose to continue their employment with BPI shall be considered in computing the ten (10)-year tenure requirement pursuant to the Retirement Plan.

The merger does not affect the tax
benefits enjoyed under the
Retirement Plan

As long as the Merger and the consequent succession by BPI as the employer of BFSBI employees in the Retirement Plan are not prejudicial to the: (1) BPI employee-members' rights in the Retirement Plan; and (2) absorbed BFSBI employee-members' rights therein, and no part of the corpus or income of the Retirement Fund shall be used for or diverted to purposes other than for the exclusive benefit of the member-employees or their beneficiaries, this Office hereby confirms that the qualification of the BPI Group of Companies Retirement Plan under Section 32 (B) (6) (a) of the Tax Code will not be affected, thus, the: (1) retirement benefits to be received by the BFSBI employee-members shall be exempt from income tax; (2) the income of the Retirement Fund from its investments is exempt from income tax; and (3) BPI may deduct contributions to the Retirement Fund from its gross income; provided, however, that all the conditions set forth in the law, rules and regulations are complied with.

This ruling is issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation it shall be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void. HTcADC

Very truly yours,

RR No. 16-2005, as amended; BIR Ruling No. VAT-322-22

Mexico Printing Company, Inc.
Parian (Pob.), Mexico,
Pampanga, Philippines

Attention: AAA
_______________

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request for confirmation that the sale of books by Mexico Printing Company, Inc. (MPCI) is exempt from Value-Added Tax (VAT) pursuant to the provision of Republic Act (RA) No. 8047 and Section 109 of the National Internal Revenue Code (Tax Code) of 1997, as amended. DETACa

Documents submitted show that MPCI, with Taxpayer Identification Number 000-000-000-00000, is a domestic corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the Republic of the Philippines under Securities and Exchange Commission Registration No. CS200509677; that the primary purpose for which MPCI is registered is to engage in commercial printing for any person or office, private or public and as principal or agent to carry on the business as printer of newspapers, journals, magazines, books and other literary works and undertaking; that MPCI is a registered member of the National Book Development Board (NBDB) with Certificate of Registration No. 6087 having been registered as an accredited book publishing (Print and Digital), book seller (Retail, Reseller, and Wholesale) and book printer; and that MPCI is currently engaged in several contracts of exclusive distributorship with different Local Government Units and the Department of Education for the distribution of learning materials.

Hence, this request.

In reply, please be informed that Section 12 of RA No. 8047 provides tax incentives to persons or entities engaged in the book industry, viz.:

"Section 12. Incentives for Book Development. —

xxx xxx xxx

Books, magazines, periodicals, newspapers, including book publishing and printing, as well as its distribution and circulation, shall be exempt from the coverage of the expanded value-added tax law."

Moreover, Section 109 (1) (R) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended, states that:

"Sec. 109. Exempt Transactions. —

(1) Subject to the provisions of Subsection (2) hereof, the following transactions shall be exempt from the value-added tax.

xxx xxx xxx

(R) Sale, importation, printing or publication of books, and any newspaper, magazine, journal, review bulletin, or any such educational reading material covered by the UNESCO Agreement on the Importation of Educational, Scientific and Cultural Materials, including the digital or electronic format thereof: Provided, That the materials enumerated herein are not devoted principally to the publication of paid advertisements."

In relation thereto, Section 4.109-1 (B) (r) of Revenue Regulations (RR) No. 16-2005, as amended, states that: aScITE

"Section 4.109-1. VAT-exempt Transactions. —

xxx xxx xxx

(B) Subject to the provisions of Section 4.109.2 hereof, the following transactions shall be exempt from VAT:

xxx xxx xxx

(r) Sale, importation, printing or publication of books, and any newspaper, magazine, journal, review bulletin, or any such educational reading material covered by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) Agreement on the importation of educational, scientific and cultural materials, including the digital or electronic format thereof. Provided, That the materials enumerated herein are not devoted principally to the publication of paid advertisements. Provided, further, That the materials enumerated herein are compliant with the requirements set forth by the National Book Development Board pursuant to R.A. No. 8047."

In view of the foregoing, this Office confirms that MPCI is exempt from the twelve percent (12%) VAT on its sale, importation, printing or publication of books, and any newspaper, magazine, journal, review bulletin, or any such educational reading material covered by the UNESCO Agreement on the Importation of Educational, Scientific and Cultural Materials, including the digital or electronic format thereof, provided that the materials enumerated herein are not devoted principally to the publication of paid advertisements; and are compliant with the requirements set forth by the NBDB pursuant to RA No. 8047.

Accordingly, in case the government made a purchase of MPCI's' products, the former shall no longer withhold and remit to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) the five percent (5%) creditable withholding VAT mandated under Revenue Memorandum Order No. 23-2014, by reason of Section 109 (1) (R) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended. The operation of Section 4.114 (2) (a) of RR No. 16-2005, as amended, viz.:

"Sec. 4.114-2. Withholding of VAT on Government Money Payments and Payments to Non Residents. —

(a) The government or any of its political subdivisions, instrumentalities or agencies, including government-owned or controlled corporations (GOCCs) shall, before making payment on account of each purchase of goods and/or of services which are subject to the value-added tax imposed in Secs. 106 and 108 of this Code, deduct and withhold a final value-added tax at the rate of five percent (5%) of the gross payment thereof: provided, that beginning January 1, 2021, the VAT withholding system under this subsection shall shift from final to a creditable system;"

xxx xxx xxx

finds no application to such transaction between MPCI and the government due to the exemption granted to the former predicated under the provision of Section 109 (1) (R) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended.

It is worth noting, however, that if MPCI is engaged in other non-exempt activities such as the printing of brochures, bookbinding, engraving, stereotyping, electrotyping, lithographing of various reference books, trade books, journals and other literary works, said transactions are subject to VAT, and the taxpayer, shall be required to register its business as VAT business entity and must issue a separate VAT invoice therefor to record the same. CAIHTE

It bears stressing that VAT is an indirect tax payable by the seller and not the purchaser of goods. Being an indirect tax, it can be shifted or passed on to the buyer/purchaser, transferee or lessee of the goods, properties or services. Once shifted to the buyer/customer as an addition to the cost of goods or services sold, it is no longer a tax but an additional cost which the buyer/customer has to pay in order to obtain the goods or services. Thus, the shifting of the VAT to MPCI does not make it the person directly liable and therefore, it cannot invoke its tax exemption privilege under Section 109 (1) (R) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended, to avoid the passing on or shifting of the VAT. Hence, its purchase of goods, properties, or services from its suppliers shall nevertheless be subject to the 12% VAT pursuant to Section 107 of the same Code.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be ascertained that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void. HTcADC

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Department of Agriculture
Elliptical Road, Diliman, Quezon City, 1101

Attention: Bernie Ferrer Cruz
Administrator

Gentlemen :

This pertains to PCA's letter requesting for the classification of coconut sugar as raw sugar and consequently, be considered as value-added tax (VAT) exempt agricultural product, pursuant to Section 109 (1) (A) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended (Tax Code), which states:

"SEC. 109. Exempt Transactions. —

(1) Subject to the provisions of Subsection (2) hereof, the following transactions shall exempt from the value-added tax.

(A) Sale or importation of agricultural and marine food products in their original state, livestock and poultry of a kind generally used as, or yielding or producing foods for human consumption; and breeding stock and genetic materials therefor.

Products classified under this paragraph shall be considered in their original state even if they have undergone the simple processes of preparation or preservation for the market, such as freezing, drying, salting, broiling, roasting, smoking or stripping. Polished and/or husked rice, corn grits, raw cane sugar and molasses, ordinary salt and copra shall be considered in their original state;" (Emphasis and underscoring supplied)

As represented, in the case of coconut sugar, the production process involves the collection of coconut sap by tapping the unopened inflorescence of the coconut palm and boiling it until granules are formed. Coconut sap sugar production is a simple farm-level technology involving a natural process of heat evaporation to convert liquid sap to a solid form of sugar granules. As alleged, this process is similar to and even simpler than the production of raw cane sugar such as muscovado, which is VAT-exempt. aScITE

As further alleged, attached to your letter are laboratory tests of coconut sap sugar samples from different producers revealing "polarimeter readings of 87.98º and below which are lesser than 99.5º and colors of 12,658 ICU and higher which are greater than 800 ICU."

Therefore, based on the evaluation of the production process of coconut sugar, the PCA is of the opinion that coconut sugar may be regarded in its original state, similar treatment to that of muscovado, and hence, can be exempt from the imposition of VAT.

In reply, it is important to point out that Section 109 (1) (A) of the Tax Code clearly states that for agricultural food products, which the coconut falls under, the sale or importation of such products is exempt from VAT if in their original state. Thus, the sale or importation of a coconut fruit, which is in its original state, is VAT-exempt.

The same Section 109 (1) (A), however, provides for an exception. It further states that "products classified under this paragraph shall be considered in their original state even if they have undergone the simple processes of preparation or preservation for the market, such as freezing, drying, salting, broiling, roasting, smoking or stripping. Polished and/or husked rice, corn grits, raw cane sugar and molasses, ordinary salt and copra shall be considered in their original state;"

In the process flow of Coconut Sap Sugar attached to your letter, the following are performed, which includes "boiling": CAIHTE

— Unopened inflorescence

— Sap Collection

— Sap Straining

— Boiling up to 115ºC — Removal of Scum — Scum

— Sap Syrup

— Boiling up to 115ºC

— Removal from Heat with Continuous Stirring

— Moist Coconut Sugar

— Sieving and Drying

— Coconut Sugar

Although Section 109 (1) (A) of the Tax Code does not specifically mention "boiling" under one of the simple processes, Revenue Regulations (RR) No. 8-2015, [1] applicable to "raw cane sugar," specifies the following process which includes boiling, and which is considered VAT-exempt:

"(a) Raw Cane Sugar — the natural sugar extracted from sugarcane through simple mechanical process by pressing for the juice; boiled to crystallize; filtered using centrifuge to separate these crystals, and dried, resulting to crystallize brown sugar (brown color due to natural molasses content present in sugar cane); Provided, that it shall refer to raw cane sugar produced from conducting only one (1) stage of filtering and centrifugal without any other further process applied thereto, such as but not limited to washing, bleaching, etc.: Provided further, that its color is greater than 800 ICU and that its content of sucrose by weight in dry state corresponds to a polarimeter reading of less than 99.5º.

The above definition includes muscovado which has standard specifications as produced, namely: Powder Class A — polarization of 86º minimum; Powder Class B — polarization of 77º minimum: and, Lump — polarization of 57º minimum.

Thus, only those falling under the above-definition of Raw Cane Sugar, including muscovado, are exempt from VAT, or from Percentage Tax, pursuant to Section 109 (1)(A) of the Tax Code."

Based on the foregoing, the coconut sap sugar samples which underwent the process described above, and which have "polarimeter readings of 87.98º and below which are lesser than 99.5º and colors of 12.658 ICU and higher which are greater than 800 ICU," appear to have met the requirements of Section 109 (1) (A) of the Tax Code, for agricultural food products to be considered in their original state. Moreover, the following enumeration in the last part of Section 109 (1) (A) — "Polished and/or husked rice, corn grits, raw cane sugar and molasses, ordinary salt and copra shall be considered in their original state" — does not appear to be exclusive. It merely states that the items in the list shall be considered in their original state.

Thus, the coconut sap sugar samples which underwent the process described above, and which have "polarimeter readings of 87.98º and below which are lesser than 99.5º and colors of 12.658 ICU and higher which are greater than 800 ICU," are agricultural food products considered to be in their original state, and are considered VAT-exempt agricultural food products, pursuant to Section 109 (1) (A) of the Tax Code.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered void. HTcADC

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request on behalf of Shizen, Inc. ("Shizen") for confirmation that:

1. Shizen, being a renewable energy ("RE") developer, is subject to zero percent (0%) value-added tax ("VAT") on its: (a) lease of certain premises used for installation and maintenance of solar power plant, generation and distribution of power from solar energy sources, and other related activities necessary and incidental thereto; and (b) purchases of local supplies, properties, and services needed for the development, construction, and installation of the Palauig Solar Power Project, pursuant to Section 15 (g) par. 2 of Republic Act (RA) No. 9513; and

2. To be entitled to the zero percent (0%) VAT, Shizen is only required to submit to the lessor and its other suppliers a copy of its Department of Energy ("DOE") and Board of Investments ("BOI") registrations pursuant to Revenue Regulations (RR) No. 7-2022. aScITE

Background

1. Shizen (Taxpayer Identification Number: 000-000-000-000) [1] is a domestic corporation duly registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") under SEC Registration No. CS201817537 on August 15, 2018, with primary purpose of engaging in the exploration, development, construction and any other allied activities to engage in any work upon manufacturing plants, solar energy generating plants.

2. Shizen is registered with the DOE under Registration No. SEOC 2022-01-607 (formerly 2019-03-518) dated March 2, 2022 as an RE developer of Solar Power Project (the "Project") located in Palauig, Zambales.

3. Shizen was registered with the BOI under BOI Certificate of Registration No. 2020-160 dated September 9, 2020.

4. Under Shizen's DOE and BOI registrations, it enjoys the privilege of zero percent VAT rate on its purchases of local supply of goods, properties, and services needed for the development, construction, and installation of its plant facilities and the whole process of exploration and development of RE sources up to conversion into power.

5. On January 30, 2020, Shizen and Philippine Radio Educational and Information Center, Inc. ("PREIC") entered into a Land Lease Agreement ("Lease Agreement") for the lease of various premises located in Barangay Lipay, Municipality of Palauig, Province of Zambales, consisting of approximately 102.181 hectares (the "Leased Premises").

6. Pursuant to the Lease Agreement, Shizen shall solely use the Leased Premises for the installation and maintenance of a solar power plant, the generation and distribution of power from solar energy sources, and other related activities necessary and incidental thereto. The annual rent shall be PhP__________ per hectare, a fraction of a hectare to be paid proportionately, subject to two percent (2%) annual increase every anniversary date. Any VAT due shall be shouldered by Shizen and shall be added to the amount payable. CAIHTE

In reply, please be informed that Section 15 (g) of RA No. 9513 reads:

"SEC. 15. Incentives for Renewable Energy Projects and Activities. — RE Developers of renewable energy facilities, including hybrid systems, in proportion to and to the extent of the RE component, for both power and non-power applications, as duly certified by the DOE, in consultation with the BOI, shall be entitled to the following incentives:

xxx xxx xxx

(g) Zero Percent Value-Added Tax Rate. —

xxx xxx xxx

All RE Developers shall be entitled to zero-rated value-added tax on its purchases of local supply of goods, properties and services needed for the development, construction and installation of its plant facilities.

This provision shall also apply to the whole process of exploring and developing renewable energy sources up to its conversion into power, including but not limited to the services performed by subcontractors and/or contractors." (Underscoring supplied)

In relation thereto, Section 108 (B) (3) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, provides that:

"Sec. 108. Value-Added Tax on Sale of Services and Use or Lease of Properties. —

xxx xxx xxx

(B) Transactions Subject to Zero Percent (0%) Rate. — The following services performed in the Philippines by VAT registered persons shall be subject to zero percent (0%) rate:

xxx xxx xxx

(3) Services rendered to persons or entities whose exemption under special laws or international agreements to which the Philippines is a signatory effectively subjects the supply of such services to zero percent (0%) rate;

xxx xxx xxx"

Based on the foregoing provisions, it is evident that the intention of the legislators is to exclude RE developers from the coverage of the 12% VAT on their local purchases of goods, properties, and services needed for the development, construction and installation of their power plant facilities, including the whole process of exploring and developing renewable energy sources up to its conversion into power. Please note that the covered transactions also include lease of goods, properties, and services, provided that they are related to the development, construction and installation of power plant facilities.

Accordingly, the suppliers/sellers/lessors of goods, properties, and services of Shizen, it being a DOE-certified RE Developer, should not pass on 12% VAT to the latter's purchases/lease of goods, properties, and services relating to the Project. It must be emphasized, however, that the zero-percent (0%) VAT shall be limited only to Shizen's local purchases/lease of goods, properties, and services that will be used in its development, construction and installation of the Project. [2]

Likewise, the grant of VAT zero-rating shall be subject to post audit verification by the Bureau of Internal Revenue ("BIR") whether the leased/purchased goods/properties/services were indeed utilized in the development, construction and installation of Project.

This ruling is issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation it shall be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void. HTcADC

(SGD.) LARRY M. BARCELO [3]
Assistant Commissioner
Legal Service

This refers to your letter, applying on behalf of F.E.I.H. SCHOOL OF MAKATI, INC. for the issuance of a certificate of tax exemption enjoyed by a non-stock, non-profit corporation or association organized and operated exclusively for educational purposes under Section 30 (H) of the National Internal Revenue Code (Tax Code) of 1997, as amended.

It is represented that F.E.I.H. SCHOOL OF MAKATI, INC. with Taxpayer's Identification No. 000-000-000-000 and Certificate of Registration No. OCN 9RC0000558236 dated August 29, 2001, is a non-stock, non-profit association duly organized and existing under the laws of the Republic of the Philippines; that it is registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission under Company Registration No. A200111202; and that the primary purpose [1] for which the association was incorporated is to establish and operate a non-stock and non-profit educational institution or learning center which shall provide courses of study in Pre-school/Elementary and High School subject to the laws of the Philippines; and that it was granted a Certificate of Good Standing by the Department of Education National Capital Region on December 5, 2022. aScITE

In reply, please be informed that paragraph 3, Section 4, Article XIV of the 1987 Constitution states that:

"All revenues and assets of non-stock, non-profit educational institutions used actually, directly, and exclusively for educational purposes shall be exempt from taxes and duties."

Similarly, Section 30 (H) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended, provides, viz.:

"Sec. 30. Exempt from Tax on Corporations. — The following organizations shall not be taxed under this Title in respect to income received by them as such:

xxx xxx xxx

(H) A non-stock and non-profit educational institution; x x x."

Moreover, there are two requisites in order for a non-stock, non-profit educational institution to be exempt from tax as provided under Revenue Memorandum Order No. 44-2016; to wit:

a) It is a non-stock, non-profit educational institution; and

b) Its revenues are actually, directly and exclusively used for educational purposes.

"Non-stock" means "no part of its income is distributable as dividends to its members, trustees, or officers" and that any profit "obtained as an incident to its operations shall, whenever necessary or proper, be used for the furtherance of the purpose or purposes for which the corporation was organized." [2] "Non-profit" means that "no net income or asset accrues to or benefits any member or specific person, with all the net income or asset devoted to the institution's purposes and all its activities conducted not for profit." [3]

In the submitted documents of F.E.I.H. SCHOOL OF MAKATI, INC., it was disclosed in the 2021 Annual Financial Statement that the Fringe Benefit covers 40% of its operating expenses, and that there was no such expense in the previous years. In addition, the President's Affidavit/Certification states that most of these benefits went to the teachers and staff allowances, bonus and incentives, including a quarter's allowance for its personnel. CAIHTE

The giving of too many allowances and incentives to the teachers and staff of the institution is considered as distribution of equity (including the net income) of F.E.I.H. SCHOOL OF MAKATI, INC. This is a form of private inurement which the law prohibits in the organization and operation of a non-stock, non-profit corporation. This act violates the requirement that no part of the net income or assets of the corporation shall inure to the benefit of any individual or specific person. Thus, F.E.I.H. SCHOOL OF MAKATI INC. cannot be qualified as a non-stock, non-profit educational institution under Section 30 (H) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended.

Please bear in mind that, "being a non-stock and/or non-profit corporation does not, by this reason alone, completely exempt an institution from tax." [4] Thus, "statutes granting tax exemptions are construed strictissimi juris against the taxpayer and liberally in favor of the taxing authority. A claim of tax exemption must be clearly shown and based on language in law too plain to be mistaken. Otherwise stated, taxation is the rule, exemption is the exception. The burden of proof rests upon the party claiming the exemption to prove that it is in fact covered by the exemption so claimed." [5] (BIR Ruling No. 466-2014 dated November 19, 2014)

In view of the foregoing, the request of F.E.I.H. SCHOOL OF MAKATI, INC. to be exempted from income tax on its income as a Section 30 (H) institution is hereby denied as it failed to prove that it is a non-profit corporation. Therefore, F.E.I.H. SCHOOL OF MAKATI, INC. shall be treated as a proprietary educational institution subject to ten percent (10%) preferential rate pursuant to Section 27 (B) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended. HTcADC

Please be guided accordingly.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Dear Madame :

This refers to your letter requesting for confirmation that the transfer of conjugal properties in your name and your common children by reason of Declaration of Nullity of Marriage is not subject to capital gains tax (CGT), documentary stamp tax (DST) and/or donor's tax. cSEDTC

Background:

It is represented that you were previously married to BBB (BBB). However, in 2011, you filed a petition for Declaration of Nullity of Marriage entitled "AAA vs. BBB" in Civil Case No. 11-126932. Thereafter, a decision granting the petition was issued by the Regional Trial Court of Manila-Branch 38 on October 25, 2016 and attained finality on August 22, 2017. During the course of the marriage, the following properties were acquired:

1. a townhouse located at Sta. Cruz, Manila under Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) No. 285998 of the Registry of Deeds of Manila;

2. a condominium unit at Avida San Lazaro Tower 4, Sta. Cruz, Manila under Condominium Certificate of Title (CCT) No. 002-2021009611 of the Registry of Deeds of Manila;

3. a house and lot located in Bloomfields Subdivision, Novaliches, Quezon City, under TCT No. 277269 of the Registry of Deeds of Quezon City; and

4. a lot located in Northfields Subdivision, Malolos, Bulacan, under TCT No. T-149798 of the Registry of Deeds of West Bulacan.

Collectively, these shall be referred to as "the Properties."

Likewise, in the same decision, the Court forfeited the share of BBB in favor of the common children, pursuant to par. 4 of Article 147 of the Family Code of the Philippines, wherein the share in the co-ownership of the guilty spouse in a void marriage shall be forfeited in favor of the common children. The court also ordered that his share be equally divided and be transferred and registered under the names of his children, namely, CCC, DDD, and EEE. Thus, this request for confirmation.

Discussion:

In reply, please be informed as follows:

Section 24 (D) (1) of the National Internal Revenue Code (Tax Code) of 1997, as amended, provides: TIADCc

"(D) Capital Gains from Sale of Real Property. —

(1) In General. — The provisions of Section 39(B) notwithstanding, a final tax of six percent (6%) based on the gross selling price of current fair market value as determined in accordance with Section 6(E) of this Code, whichever is higher, is hereby imposed upon capital gains presumed to have been realized from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of real property located in the Philippines, classified as capital assets, including pacto de retro sales and other forms of conditional sales, by individuals, including estates and trusts: Provided, That the tax liability, if any, on gains from sales or other dispositions of real property to the government or any of its political subdivisions or agencies or to government-owned or controlled corporations shall be determined either under Section 24 (A) or under this Subsection, at the option of taxpayer; x x x"

Considering that the transfer, adjudication, or distribution of the above-mentioned conjugal properties in your favor is not pursuant to a sale, hence, without monetary consideration, the said transfer, adjudication, or distribution is therefore not subject to the CGT imposed under the above-mentioned provision. Neither is the said transfer, adjudication, or distribution subject to the donor's tax imposed under Section 98 of the same Tax Code; there being no donative intent on your part or that of BBB because the transfer, adjudication, or distribution is made only in compliance with your property settlement, which was approved by the court.

It must be emphasized, however, that the Properties acquired by both parties must be divided equally between them in order not to consider the distribution as conveyance of property but simply as partition or segregation of that part of the property that belongs to the co-owners. Should one co-owner get a share more than the other co-owner, the excess thereof is considered "other disposition" of property subject to CGT and DST under Section 24 (D) (1) of the Tax Code of 1997, as amended (BIR Ruling No. 377-2017 dated August 14, 2017).

The adjudication of the Properties to the children shall be considered a delivery of their presumptive legitimes pursuant to Article 50 of the Family Code, as amended, and therefore not subject to the CGT imposed under the above-mentioned provision. However, an annotation of the transmission of such properties to the children as their presumptive legitimes must be made in the corresponding TCTs covering such realties, for estate tax purposes. The said properties being considered as advances on the children's legitimes pursuant to Article 51 of the Family Code, as amended, shall be included as part of the gross estate and subject to the estate tax, if any, upon the death of either you or BBB. The Properties shall be included in your and BBB's estate, divided equally, as said Properties are co-owned.

Finally, the transfer of the properties in your name, BBB and your common children, made in accordance with the court decision, is not subject to DST pursuant to Section 185 of Revenue Regulations No. 26, otherwise known as the Revised Documentary Stamp Regulations, which provides that the conveyance of a real property without monetary consideration is not subject to the payment of DST. The notarial certification is, however, subject to the DST of fifteen pesos (P15.00) [1] imposed under Section 188 of the Same Code (BIR Ruling No. 633-2012 dated November 26, 2012 and BIR Ruling No. 377-2017 dated August 14, 2017).

Conclusion:

In sum, the transfer of the conjugal properties in your name and your common children by reason of the Declaration of Nullity of Marriage with BBB is not subject to CGT, DST, and/or donor's tax.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void. ETHIDa

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

TERMS AND CONDITIONS
OF THE CERTIFICATE OF TAX EXEMPTION

For Non-Stock, Non-Profit Educational Institution
under Section 30 (H) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as Amended

TAX EXEMPTION

1) INCOME TAX. ANTIQUE CHRISTIAN CENTER, INC. is exempt from the payment of income tax only on revenues and receipts enumerated on the Certificate of Tax Exemption. It is understood that the school must continue to meet the following requisites as set forth under Revenue Memorandum Order (RMO) No. 44-2016, to wit: CAIHTE

i. It is a non-stock, non-profit educational institution; and

ii. Its revenues are actually, directly and exclusively used for educational purposes.

ANTIQUE CHRISTIAN CENTER, INC.'s interest income from currency bank deposits and yield from deposit substitute instruments used actually, directly and exclusively in pursuance of its purpose as an educational institution, are exempt from the 20% final tax and 15% [1] tax under the expanded foreign currency deposit system imposed under Section 27 (D) (1) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, subject to compliance with the conditions that as a tax-exempt institution it shall on an annual basis submit to the Revenue District Office concerned an annual information return and duly audited financial statement together with the following:

a) Certification from their depository bank as to the amount of interest income earned from passive investment not subject to the 20% final withholding tax and 15% tax on interest income under the expanded foreign currency deposit system imposed by Section 27 (D) (1) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended;

b) Certification of actual utilization of the said income; and

c) Board Resolution by the school administration on proposed projects (i.e., construction and/or improvement of school buildings and facilities, acquisition of equipment, books and the like) to be funded out of the money deposited in banks or placed in money markets, on or before the 15th day of the fourth month following the end of its taxable year (Sec. 4, Finance Department Order No. 137-87). [2]

2) VALUE-ADDED TAX (VAT) ON EDUCATIONAL SERVICES. Pursuant to Section 109 (1) (H) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, ANTIQUE CHRISTIAN CENTER, INC.'s gross receipts from operations as a non-stock, non-profit educational institution are exempt from VAT. Moreover, revenues derived from assets used in the operation of cafeterias/canteens, dormitories and bookstores located within the premises of ANTIQUE CHRISTIAN CENTER, INC. are exempt from taxation provided they are owned and operated by it as ancillary services.

LIABILITY FOR INTERNAL REVENUE TAXES

1) INCOME TAX

ANTIQUE CHRISTIAN CENTER, INC. is subject to income tax on all its income/receipts/revenues not expressly exempted and stated in the Certificate of Tax Exemption. Moreover, it is subject to the corresponding internal revenue taxes imposed under National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, on its income derived from any of its properties, real or personal, or any activity conducted for profit, which income should be returned for taxation, unless said revenues are actually, directly and exclusively used for educational purposes. aScITE

2) VALUE-ADDED TAX/PERCENTAGE TAX

If ANTIQUE CHRISTIAN CENTER, INC. is engaged in the sale of goods or services in the course of a business pursuit, including transactions incidental thereto, its revenues derived therefrom shall be subject to the 12% VAT, in case the gross receipts from such sales exceed Three Million Pesos (P3,000,000.00), [3] or to the 3% percentage tax, if gross receipts do not exceed P3,000,000.00.

Notwithstanding that it is a non-stock, non-profit corporation, its purchase of goods or properties, services and importation of goods shall nevertheless be subject to the 12% VAT pursuant to Sections 106, 107 and 108 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended.

3) WITHHOLDING TAX

ANTIQUE CHRISTIAN CENTER, INC. shall be constituted as withholding agent for the government if it acts as an employer and its employees receive compensation income subject to the withholding tax under Section 79 (A), Chapter XIII, Title II of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 2-98, as amended, or if it makes income payments to individuals or corporations subject to the withholding tax pursuant to Section 57 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, and as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 2-98, as amended.

TAXPAYER DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

1) The honoraria/allowances given to members of the Board of Trustees must be reasonable and subject to liquidation (DOF Opinion No. 005-2019).

2) Required to file on or before the 15th day of the fourth month following the end of the accounting period a Profit and Loss Statement and Balance Sheet with the Annual Information Return under oath, stating its gross income and expenses incurred during the preceding period and a certificate showing that there has not been any change in its By-laws, Articles of Incorporation, manner of operation and activities as well as sources and disposition of income. Copy of this Certificate of Tax Exemption shall be attached to the aforementioned Annual Information Return.

3) Under Section 235 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, any provision of existing general and special law to the contrary notwithstanding, the books of accounts and other pertinent records of tax-exempt organizations or grantees of tax incentives shall be subject to examination by the BIR for purposes of ascertaining compliance with the conditions under which it has been granted tax exemptions or tax incentives, and its tax liabilities, if any. DETACa

4) Further, it is also required under Section 6 (C) in relation to Section 237 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, to issue duly registered receipts or sales or commercial invoices for each sale or transfer of merchandise or for services rendered which are not directly related to the activities for which the Association is registered. (Revenue Memorandum Circular [RMC] No. 76-2003)

5) Finally, it is subject to the payment of registration fee of PhP500.00 as prescribed in Section 236 (B) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended.

Details.Details:
Sections 24 (D) (1), 98, 99, 101, 173, 188, 196 and 199 of the
National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended;
Section 132 (e) of Republic Act (RA) No. 7653 and
Section 66 of RA No. 6657; BIR Ruling M-170-2021

Bureau of Treasury
Ayuntamiento Building, Cabildo St. cor. A. Soriano Avenue,
Intramuros, Manila 1002

Attention: Rosalia V. De Leon
Treasurer of the Philippines

Eduardo Anthony G. Mariño, III
Deputy Treasurer of the Philippines

Gentlemen :

This refers to your letter requesting for an exemption from the payment of National Taxes imposed on the transfer of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP)-covered Central Bank-Board of Liquidators (CB-BOL) real properties as the disposition of the said properties to the National Government (NG) is by deed of assignment and not through sales transaction. caITAC

It is represented that CB-BOL, constituted pursuant to Section 132 (e) of Republic Act (RA) No. 7653 or the New Central Bank Act, ceased its operation on June 2018. The CB-BOL assigned its undisposed assets to the NG through the Bureau of Treasury (BTr). It was pointed out that these are "gratuitous assignments" effected through the execution of various Deeds of Assignment in an "as-is-where-is" basis.

It was stated that among those assigned to BTr are real properties covered under the CARP. These properties were yet to be titled in favor of the Republic of the Philippines or the State. The subject properties were grouped into two as stated in the BTr's letter dated April 26, 2023: (1) Deed of Assignment (DOA) between CB-BOL and the Republic of the Philippines (ROP) through the BTr, which pertains to forty-four (44) properties; and (2) DOA between CB-BOL and ROP through the BTr, which pertains to ten (10) properties possibly under CARP (not indicated in DOA).

The BTr asserts that said "gratuitous assignments" are not subject to Donor's Tax, Documentary Stamp Tax (DST), and Capital Gains Tax (CGT) for the following reasons: TAIaHE

a. Donor's Tax — Section 101 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended (Tax Code) provides that gifts made to or for use of the National Government or any entity created by any of its agencies which is not conducted for profit, or to any of its political subdivisions are exempted from payment of donor's tax. As the "assignments" are gratuitous in nature, not conducted for profit, and made pursuant to each of involved agency's functions and mandate, they may be exempted from the payment of Donor's Tax.

b. DST — Section 185 of Revenue Regulations (RR) No. 26 or the DST Regulation provides that conveyances without consideration are not subject to the imposition of DST. As the "assignments" are conveyances not involving profit or those entered into without consideration, they may be exempted from the payment of DST.

c. CGT — Section 66 of RA No. 6657 or the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law of 1988 provides that "transfer of ownership covered by CARP shall be exempted from taxes arising from capital gains." As the "assignments" involves the disposition of CARP-covered properties, they may be exempted from the payment of CGT.

Hence, the BTr requests for a confirmatory ruling that the "assignments" of CARP-covered CB-BOL properties are exempt from Donor's Tax, DST, and CGT as the disposition of the said properties to the NG is by deed of assignment and are not through sales transaction.

In reply, please be informed as follows:

The Central Bank-Board of Liquidators (CB-BOL)

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) was established in 1993 to function as an independent monetary authority in an aim to bring stability to money, banking and credit. The old Central Bank of the Philippines (CBP) was dissolved to enable the new monetary authority to begin with a clean financial slate. Not all assets or liabilities of the old CBP were transferred to and assumed by the BSP pursuant to Section 132 of the RA No. 7653 or the New Central Bank Act. Those assets and liabilities which were not identified to be transferred to and assumed by the BSP remained to be the assets and liabilities of the Central Bank which continued to exist as an entity, the Central Bank-Board of Liquidators (CB-BOL). The CB-BOL's function is to administer, dispose of, and liquidate all assets and liabilities not transferred to the BSP and retained by the Board. Section 132 thereof states that:

"Section 132. Transfer of Assets and Liabilities. — Upon the effectivity of this Act, three (3) members of the Monetary Board, which may include the Governor, in representation of the Bangko Sentral, the Secretary of Finance and the Secretary of Budget and Management in representation of the National Government, and the Chairmen of the Committees on Banks of the Senate and the House of Representatives shall determine the assets and liabilities of the Central Bank which may be transferred to or assumed by the Bangko Sentral. x x x

The following guidelines shall be strictly observed in the determination of which assets and liabilities shall be transferred to the Bangko Sentral: ICHDca

xxx xxx xxx

(e) any asset or liability of the Central Bank not transferred to the Bangko Sentral shall be retained and administered, disposed of and liquidated by the Central Bank itself which shall continue to exist as the CB Board of Liquidators only for the purposes provided in this paragraph but not later than twenty-five (25) years or until such time that liabilities have been liquidated: Provided, That the Bangko Sentral may financially assist the Central Bank of Liquidators in the liquidation of CB liabilities: Provided, finally, That upon disposition of said retained assets and liquidation of said retained liabilities, the Central Bank shall be deemed abolished."

xxx xxx xxx (Emphasis Supplied)

Pursuant to the aforementioned law, Executive Order (EO) No. 169 was issued on April 17, 1994 by then President Fidel V. Ramos to reiterate the continued existence of the old Central Bank as the CB-BOL and prescribed powers and functions of the Board as well as its Chairman. The Board was not created for profit or to engage in business. The old Central Bank continued to exist as a juridical entity, known as the CB-BOL, with the specific duty of administering, disposing of, and liquidating its assets and liabilities not transferred to and assumed by the BSP. The said EO likewise authorized CB-BOL to perform such other corporate powers necessary to administer, dispose of, and liquidate the assets and liabilities retained by it and not transferred to or assumed by the BSP. Subsequent EOs issued were only for purposes of reconstituting the CB-BOL. The said Board ceased to function as the administrator and liquidator of the old Central Bank's assets and liabilities in 2018.

The Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP)

The Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program or the CARP was institutionalized through the enactment of RA No. 6657 or the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law of 1988 which aims to establish an equitable distribution and ownership of land with due consideration to just compensation for the farmers and to the improvement of agricultural productivity. The said law was mandated to be implemented and completed within ten (10) years from its effectivity or until 2008. It was extended for an additional five (5) years by RA No. 9700.

Section 66 of RA No. 6657 exempts from the payment of CGT all acts of transfer of ownership involving parcels of land identified to be under the CARP. The same section likewise exempts such acts from registration fees, and all other taxes and fees relating to the conveyance of said lands, to wit: cDHAES

"SECTION 66. Exemptions from Taxes and Fees of Land Transfers. — Transactions under this Act involving a transfer of ownership, whether from natural or juridical persons, shall be exempted from taxes arising from capital gains. These transactions shall also be exempted from the payment of registration fees, and all other taxes and fees for the conveyance or transfer thereof; Provided, That all arrearages in real property taxes, without penalty or interest, shall be deductible from the compensation to which the owner may be entitled." (Emphasis Supplied)

Donor's Tax

A donation is an act of liberality whereby a person disposes gratuitously of a thing or right in favor of another, who accepts it. On the part of the donor, it is an exercise of one's generosity. [1] In simpler terms, it is an act of a voluntary transfer of property by one to another without any consideration or compensation therefor. [2]

The essential elements of donation are as follows: (a) the essential reduction of the patrimony of the donor; (b) the increase in the patrimony of the donee; and (c) the intent to do an act of liberality or animus donandi. [3] Article 749 of the Civil Code of the Philippines further requires that the donation of a real or immovable property must be made in a public document and that the acceptance thereof be made in the same deed or in a separate public instrument. If the said acceptance is made in a separate instrument, the donor shall be notified thereof in an authentic form, and this step shall be noted in both instruments.

As for taxation, Section 98 in relation to Section 99 of the Tax Code provides that transfers by any person, resident or non-resident, by gift, of property, real or personal, are generally subject to six percent (6%) donor's tax computed on the basis of the total gifts in excess of Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P250,000.00) exempt gift made during the calendar year must be paid. Sections 98 and 99 of the Tax Code read:

"CHAPTER II — DONOR'S TAX

Section 98. Imposition of Tax. —

(A) There shall be levied, assessed, collected and paid upon the transfer by any person, resident or non-resident, of the property by gift, a tax, computed as provided in Section 99.

(B) The tax shall apply whether the transfer is in trust or otherwise, whether the gift is direct or indirect, and whether the property is real or personal, tangible or intangible.

Section 99. Rate of Tax Payable by Donor. —

(A) In General. — The tax for each calendar year shall be six percent (6%) computed on the basis of the total gifts in excess of Two hundred fifty thousand pesos (PhP250,000) exempt gift made during the calendar year. x x x" TCAScE

Further, certain gifts are exempt from donor's tax if given to qualified institutions or donee such as, among others, those made to or for the use of the National Government or any entity created by any of its agencies which is not conducted for profit, or to any political subdivision of the said Government in accordance with the conditions set under Section 101 [4] of the Tax Code.

Documentary Stamp Tax

Documentary stamp taxes (DST) are levied on the exercise by persons of certain privileges conferred by law for the creation, revision or termination of specific legal relationships through the execution of specific instruments. [5] Section 173 of the Tax Code states:

"Section 173. Stamp Taxes Upon Documents, Loan Agreements, Instruments and Papers. — Upon documents, instruments, loan agreements and papers, and upon acceptances, assignments, sales and transfers of the obligation, right or property incident thereto, there shall be levied, collected and paid for, and in respect of the transaction so had or accomplished, the corresponding documentary stamp taxes prescribed in the following Sections of this Title, by the person making, signing, issuing, accepting, or transferring the same wherever the document is made, signed, issued, accepted or transferred when the obligation or right arises from Philippine sources or the property is situated in the Philippines, and the same time such act is done or transaction had: x x x" (Emphasis Supplied)

Documents subject to DST, includes, among others, deeds or instruments involving conveyances, donations, or sale of real properties as stated in Section 196 of the same Code, to wit:

"Section 196. Stamp Tax on Deeds of Sale, Conveyances and Donation of Real Property. — On all conveyances, donations, deeds, instruments, or writings, other than grants, patents or original certificates of adjudication issued by the Government, whereby any land, tenement, or other realty sold shall be granted, assigned, transferred, donated or otherwise conveyed to the purchaser, or purchasers, or to any other person or persons designated by such purchaser or purchasers, or donee, there shall be collected a documentary stamp tax, at the rates herein below prescribed, based on the consideration contracted to be paid for such realty or on its fair market value determined in accordance with Section 6(E) of this Code, whichever is higher: x x x" (Emphasis Supplied)

Section 199 of the same Code provides for certain documents exempted from the imposition of DST including those pertaining to "contracts, deeds, documents and transactions related to the conduct of business of the BSP." ASEcHI

Capital Gains Tax

Capital Gains Tax (CGT) is a tax imposed upon the seller based on his or her presumed gain realized from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of capital assets located in the Philippines, including pacto de retro sales and other forms of conditional sale.

Section 24 (D) (1) of the Tax Code imposes a final tax of six percent (6%) upon the capital gains presumed to have been realized from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of real property located in the Philippines. The said 6% CGT is computed on the basis of the gross selling price or current fair market value, whichever is higher. Section 24 (D) (1) reads:

"Section 24. Income Tax Rates. —

xxx xxx xxx

(D) Capital Gains from Sale of Real Property. —

(1) In General. — The provisions of Section 39(B) notwithstanding, a final tax of six percent (6%) based on the gross selling price or current fair market value as determined in accordance with Section 6(E) of this Code, whichever is higher, is hereby imposed upon capital gains presumed to have been realized from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of real property located in the Philippines, classified as capital assets, including pacto de retro sales and other forms of conditional sales, by individuals, including estates and trusts: Provided, That the tax liability, if any, on gains from sales or other dispositions of real property to the government or any of its political subdivisions or agencies or to government-owned or -controlled corporations shall be determined either under Section 24(A) or under this Subsection, at the option of the taxpayer." (Emphasis supplied)

Certain transactions were executed without consideration and hence not subject to CGT. This includes, among others, the reconveyance of a real property by virtue of a Court Decision. [6] Some transactions, however, can be deemed a sales transaction, hence subject to CGT. Dacion en Pago is the transmission of the ownership of a thing by the debtor to the creditor as an accepted equivalent of the performance of obligation. [7] It is regarded as a special mode of payment wherein the debtor offers a particular thing or property to the creditor who accepts such for the settlement of a particular obligation or debt. [8] The Supreme Court viewed this as a transaction which partakes the nature of sale — i.e., the creditor is really buying the thing or property of the debtor, payment for which is to be charged against the debtor's debt. [9]

Application

In applying the foregoing, the various DOAs executed by the CB-BOL as ASSIGNOR in favor of the ROP, as represented by the BTr, as ASSIGNEE, cannot be considered a gift or donation as these were executed ultimately as a form of partial settlement of the CB-BOL's obligations or debts owed to the NG. Most of the DOAs include a provision stating that it was executed "x x x . . . and for the partial settlement of the ASSIGNOR's obligation x x x . . . the said ASSIGNOR does hereby ASSIGN, TRANSFER, CONVEY and DELIVER in a manner absolute and irrevocable x x x . . ." while some DOAs contain a provision stating that "By this assignment, the liabilities of the ASSIGNOR to the ASSIGNEE shall be reduced by an amount equivalent to x x x . . . ." Both provisions, as worded, indicate that the assignments were not at all gratuitous, as they indicate a transmission of the ownership of a thing by the debtor to the creditor as an accepted equivalent of the performance of an obligation or settlement of a debt. Hence, the DOAs cannot fall within the ambit of Sections 98 and 99 of the Tax Code. cTDaEH

The DOAs cannot also be taken as a deed or contract related to the conduct of business of the BSP for it to be exempted from DST as stated under Section 199 (l) of the same Code. The BSP and CB-BOL are separate legal entities. The CB-BOL is not under the BSP. Another view, on the contrary, defeats the purpose of establishing an independent monetary authority premised upon a clean financial slate.

As already stated, the DOAs contain a provision that shows that the penultimate goal of the assignment is the transmission of the ownership of a thing by the debtor to the creditor as an accepted equivalent of the performance of an obligation or settlement of a debt. The intent to transfer ownership is supported by the fact that the letter of request for exemption indicated that the BTr is already coordinating with the concerned agencies for the annotation and eventual titling. The abovementioned provisions make the DOAs similar to a Dacion en Pago, which partakes the nature of a sale.

Therefore, the DOAs, being in the nature of a Dacion en Pago, should have been subject to the payment of CGT and DST. However, since Section 132 (e) of RA No. 7653, or the New Central Bank Act, does not limit the manner of the disposition of properties by CB-BOL to those which will generate revenue for the NG, it is not expected to make a profit or to engage in business. Hence, by transferring its assets through the DOAs to the NG or ROP or the State as represented by the BTr, it is merely performing its mandated functions as a national government entity under EO No. 169, s. 1994, which was issued in accordance with Section 132 (e) of RA No. 7653.

Since the CB-BOL is deemed to be performing a governmental function in the transfer of its assets to the NG or ROP or the State, even if such acts contemplate a partial settlement of its obligation, the said DOAs are not subject to CGT and DST. It does not matter whether the properties transferred were under the CARP or not. Further, Section 132 (e) of RA No. 7653 provides that the CBP shall continue to exist as the CB-BOL until all retained assets or liabilities, or those not transferred to the BSP, has been administered, disposed of, and liquidated. Therefore, the CBP-BOL, being the CBP, is similarly entitled to the tax exemptions provided to the CBP [10] under RA No. 265. [11] As such, the DOAs transferring real properties from CB-BOL to the Republic of the Philippines are exempt from taxes. ITAaHc

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation it will be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

TAX EXEMPTION

1) INCOME TAX. ST. PAUL COLLEGE, ISLAND PARK, INC. is exempt from the payment of income tax only on revenues and receipts enumerated on the Certificate of Tax Exemption. It is understood that the school must continue to meet the following requisites as set forth under Revenue Memorandum Order (RMO) No. 44-2016, to wit:

i. It is a non-stock, non-profit educational institution; and

ii. Its revenues are actually, directly and exclusively used for educational purposes.

ST. PAUL COLLEGE, ISLAND PARK, INC.'s interest income from currency bank deposits and yield from deposit substitute instruments used actually, directly and exclusively in pursuance of its purpose as an educational institution, are exempt from the 20% final tax and 15% [1] tax under the expanded foreign currency deposit system imposed under Section 27 (D) (1) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, subject to compliance with the conditions that as a tax-exempt institution it shall on an annual basis submit to the Revenue District Office concerned an annual information return and duly audited financial statement together with the following:

a) Certification from their depository bank as to the amount of interest income earned from passive investment not subject to the 20% final withholding tax and 15% tax on interest income under the expanded foreign currency deposit system imposed by Section 27 (D) (1) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended.

b) Certification of actual utilization of the said income; and

c) Board Resolution by the school administration on proposed projects (i.e., construction and/or improvement of school buildings and facilities, acquisition of equipment, books and the like) to be funded out of the money deposited in banks or placed in money markets, on or before the 15th day of the fourth month following the end of its taxable year (Sec. 4, Finance Department Order No. 137-87). [2] CAIHTE

2) VALUE-ADDED TAX (VAT) ON EDUCATIONAL SERVICES. Pursuant to Section 109 (1) (H) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, ST. PAUL COLLEGE, ISLAND PARK, INC.'s gross receipts from operations as a non-stock, non-profit educational institution are exempt from VAT. Moreover, revenues derived from assets used in the operation of cafeterias/canteens, dormitories and bookstores located within the premises of ST. PAUL COLLEGE, ISLAND PARK, INC. are exempt from taxation provided they are owned and operated by it as ancillary services.

LIABILITY FOR INTERNAL REVENUE TAXES

1) INCOME TAX

ST. PAUL COLLEGE, ISLAND PARK, INC. is subject to income tax on all its income/receipts/revenues not expressly exempted and stated in the Certificate of Tax Exemption. Moreover, it is subject to the corresponding internal revenue taxes imposed under National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, on its income derived from any of its properties, real or personal, or any activity conducted for profit, which income should be returned for taxation, unless said revenues are actually, directly and exclusively used for educational purposes.

2) VALUE-ADDED TAX/PERCENTAGE TAX

If ST. PAUL COLLEGE, ISLAND PARK, INC. is engaged in the sale of goods or services in the course of a business pursuit, including transactions incidental thereto, its revenues derived therefrom shall be subject to the 12% VAT, in case the gross receipts from such sales exceed Three Million Pesos (P3,000,000.00), [3] or to the 3% percentage tax, if gross receipts do not exceed P3,000,000.00. aScITE

Notwithstanding that it is a non-stock, non-profit corporation, its purchase of goods or properties, services and importation of goods shall nevertheless be subject to the 12% VAT pursuant to Sections 106, 107 and 108 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended.

3) WITHHOLDING TAX

ST. Details.Details:
Sections 28 (B) (1), 42 (C) (3), and 108
of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) of 1997,
as amended; BIR Ruling Nos. 173-21, 297-11

Anti-Money Laundering Council
Room 507, 5/F, EDPC Building,
Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Complex,
Malate, Manila

Attention: Matthew M. David
Executive Director

Gentlemen :

This refers to your request for a ruling confirming that payments to AAA (Consultant), a non-resident, foreign service provider, for services rendered outside the Philippines are not subject to Philippine income tax, and consequently, to the withholding tax and value-added tax (VAT) under the Renewal Contract, Consultancy Services Agreement, and other subsequent renewals and agreements, the purpose of which is the removal of the Philippines from the "Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Greylist" as well as from the European Union's List of Jurisdictions with Strategic AML/CFT Deficiencies (EU List on AML/CFT). HTcADC

Background

1. The Consultant is a Canadian resident, with office address at _______________, Canada.

2. The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) entered into a Consultancy Services Agreement with the Consultant which is valid for a period of nine (9) months, starting June 10, 2020 to February 28, 2021, renewable at the option of the AMLC.

3. The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) issued BIR Ruling No. VAT-173-21 which confirmed that the income payments made to the Consultant by AMLC for services rendered abroad or outside the Philippines are not subject to Philippine income tax, withholding tax, and VAT.

4. On February 26, 2021, a Renewal Contract was executed wherein the Consultant and AMLC agreed to renew the Consultancy Services Agreement under the same terms and conditions which will cover a period of four (4) months commencing from March 1, 2021 until June 30, 2021. The said contract was renewable at the option of the AMLC subject to the execution of another Agreement.

5. On June 25, 2021, the Philippines was included in the FATF's List of Jurisdictions Under Increased Monitoring ("Grey List") which meant that the country needs to implement a list of action plan items and submit periodic progress reports to the Asia Pacific-Joint Group in January, May, and September of every year until the Philippines exits the Grey List.

6. The inclusion of the Philippines in the Grey List led to the execution of another Consultancy Services Agreement for availing the services of the Consultant for another period from September 1, 2021 to February 28, 2022.

7. The services of the Consultant may be renewed continuously for period of six (6) months until the Philippines exits the International Cooperation Review Group Active Review Process, at the option of the AMLC, subject to the execution of another Agreement. All services under the subsequent Agreement shall be under the same terms and conditions of the Consultancy Service Agreement executed on September 1, 2021. CAIHTE

8. All services under the Renewal Contract and the Consultancy Services Agreement executed on February 26, 2021 and September 1, 2021 respectively were rendered outside the Philippines, including desk-based reviews, email correspondences, video conferences, and virtual/online delivery workshops.

Hence, this request.

In reply, please be informed that Sections 23 (D) and 25 (B) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended (Tax Code) provide:

"SEC. 23. General Principles of Income Taxation in the Philippines. — Except when otherwise provided in this Code:

xxx xxx xxx

(D) An alien individual, whether a resident or not of the Philippines, is taxable only on income derived from sources within the Philippines;"

"SEC. 25. Tax on Nonresident Alien Individual. —

xxx xxx xxx

(B) Nonresident Alien Individual Not Engaged in Trade or Business within the Philippines. — There shall be levied, collected and paid for each taxable year upon the entire income received from all sources within the Philippines by every nonresident alien individual not engaged in trade or business within the Philippines as . . . salaries, wages, . . . compensation, remuneration, . . . a tax equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of such income. . ."

In relation to the previously cited provisions, Section 42 (A) (3) and (C) (3) of the Tax Code states that compensation for labor or personal services is derived from sources within the Philippines if the services are performed therein, and outside if the services are performed outside the Philippines, to wit:

"SEC. 42. Income from Sources within the Philippines. —

(A) Gross Income from Sources within the Philippines. — The following items of gross income shall be treated as gross income from sources within the Philippines:

xxx xxx xxx

(3) Services. — Compensation for labor or personal services performed in the Philippines;

xxx xxx xxx

(C) Gross Income from Sources without the Philippines. — The following items of gross income shall be treated as income from sources without the Philippines:

xxx xxx xxx

(3) Compensation for labor or personal services performed without the Philippines;"

In accordance with the aforementioned provisions, non-resident alien individuals are subject to income tax only on income derived from all sources within the Philippines. Conversely, they are not subject to income tax on income derived from sources outside the Philippines. aScITE

The Bureau reiterates the following points contained in BIR Ruling No. 212-12: [1]

"The situs of tax for services is the place where the service is rendered. Under the Philippine source of income rules for income tax purposes, service income will be considered Philippine source income only if the services are rendered in the Philippines. Conversely, if the services are rendered outside the Philippines, the service income will be considered as foreign source income. x x x

"The rule in this jurisdiction regarding tax situs is: the source of an income is the property, activity or service that produced the income; the test of taxability is the source, and the source of an income is that activity which produced the income (CIR v. British Overseas Airways Corporation, G.R. Nos. 65773-74, April 30, 1987). Stated differently, the situs of the income derived from labor or personal services is determined solely by the place where service is rendered (CIR v. Japan Airlines, Inc., G.R. No. 60714, March 6, 1991). Compensation from services performed abroad is, therefore, considered income from sources without the Philippines and thus not subject to Philippine Income tax." (Emphasis supplied.)

Applying the foregoing provisions, AAA is a non-resident alien individual not doing business in the Philippines and her professional fees or compensation constitute income derived from sources outside the Philippines, it can be said that the same are not subject to income tax, and consequently, to the withholding tax.

On the other hand, Section 108 (A) of the Tax Code clearly reads that the sale or exchange of services subject to VAT include only those services that are performed in the Philippines, viz.:

"SEC. 108. Value-Added Tax on Sale of Services and Use or Lease of Properties. —

(A) Rate and Base of Tax. — There shall be levied, assessed and collected, a value-added tax equivalent to twelve percent (12%) of gross receipts derived from the sale or exchange of services, including the use or lease of properties.

The phrase 'sale or exchange of services' means the performance of all kinds of services in the Philippines for others for a fee, remuneration of consideration. . ."

Accordingly, the service fees to be paid by the AMLC to AAA, to the extent that the subject services are not performed in the Philippines, are exempt from VAT. Conversely, if the subject services are performed in the Philippines, these shall be subject to VAT. DETACa

IN VIEW OF THE FOREGOING, this Office hereby CONFIRMS your opinion that the income payments made for services rendered by AAA to the AMLC under the Renewal Contract dated February 26, 2021 and the Consultancy Services Agreement dated September 1, 2021, including other subsequent renewals and agreements containing the same terms and conditions, the purpose of which is the removal of the Philippines from the "FATF Grey list" as well as from the European Union's List of Jurisdictions with Strategic AML/CFT Deficiencies (EU List on AML/CFT), are NOT subject to Philippine income tax, withholding tax, and VAT to the extent that the subject services are not performed in the Philippines. Conversely, if the subject services are performed in the Philippines, such in the case of any in-country missions or in-country trainings, these shall be subject to Philippine income tax, withholding tax, and VAT.

This ruling is being issued on the basis of the foregoing facts as represented. However, if upon investigation, it will be disclosed that the facts are different, then this ruling shall be considered null and void.

Very truly yours,

(SGD.) ROMEO D. LUMAGUI, JR.
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

1) INCOME TAX

FOOD FOR HUNGRY MINDS SCHOOL, INC. is subject to income tax on all its income/receipts/revenues not expressly exempted and stated in the Certificate of Tax Exemption. Moreover, it is subject to the corresponding internal revenue taxes imposed under the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, on its income derived from any of its properties, real or personal, or any activity conducted for profit, which income should be returned for taxation, unless said revenues are actually, directly and exclusively used for educational purposes.

2) VALUE-ADDED TAX/PERCENTAGE TAX

If FOOD FOR HUNGRY MINDS SCHOOL, INC. is engaged in the sale of goods or services in the course of a business pursuit, including transactions incidental thereto, its revenues derived therefrom shall be subject to the 12% VAT, in case the gross receipts from such sales exceed Three Million Pesos (P3,000,000.00), [3] or to the 3% percentage tax, if gross receipts do not exceed P3,000,000.00.

Notwithstanding that it is a non-stock, non-profit corporation, its purchase of goods or properties, services and importation of goods shall nevertheless be subject to the 12% VAT pursuant to Sections 106, 107 and 108 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended.

3) WITHHOLDING TAX

FOOD FOR HUNGRY MINDS SCHOOL, INC. shall be constituted as withholding agent for the government if it acts as an employer and its employees receive compensation income subject to the withholding tax under Section 79 (A), Chapter XIII, Title II of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 2-98, as amended, or if it makes income payments to individuals or corporations subject to the withholding tax pursuant to Section 57 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, and as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 2-98, as amended.
